title: Super Resolution Reconstruction: A Strategy to Improve the Diagnostic Performance of Radiomics for Predicting Microvascular Invasion in Hepatocellular Carcinoma.
abstract: Rationale and objectives Microvascular invasion (MVI) is a key factor associated with high postoperative recurrence rate in patients with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). This study aims to evaluate the value of super-resolution (SR) reconstruction based on hepatobiliary phase (HBP) MR images for improving the accuracy of MVI prediction. Materials and methods A total of 544 patients with HCC from two medical centers between 2018 and 2025 were retrospectively analyzed, including 450 patients in the training set, 51 in the internal validation set, and 43 in the external test set. Based on a lesion-aware 3D Restormer transformer architecture, SR reconstruction was performed using HBP MR images to generate super-resolution MR images. Tumor segmentations were automatically performed using the nnU-Net architecture and manually corrected by an experienced abdominal radiologist before radiomics feature extraction. Radiomics features were then extracted from original and SR images. Radiomics models based on original and SR images were developed to predict MVI status. Three machine learning algorithms, including Logistic Regression, Random Forest, and LightGBM, were used for model development. Results A total of 851 radiomics features were extracted from the original and SR images, respectively. Redundant features were filtered, and 50 radiomics features were selected using LASSO regression with cross-validated. For MVI prediction, the pooled areas under the receiver operating curves (AUCs) of radiomics model based on the original images were 0.710, 0.764, and 0.614 in the training, validation and test sets, respectively. The corresponding AUCs of the radiomics model based on the SR images were 0.855, 0.798, and 0.827, respectively. In the test set, the AUC of the radiomics model based on the SR images was higher than that based on the original images (0.827 vs. 0.614, p <0.001). Conclusion SR reconstruction can improve the diagnostic performance of radiomics models for predicting MVI in patients with HCC.

title: Explainable WinDWS-SwinNet: Optimizing Ultrasound Deep Radiomics for Multipathology Breast Lesion Classification.
abstract: Rationale and objectives Timely and accurate characterization of breast lesions into different pathological classes through noninvasive imaging techniques is crucial for early cancer diagnosis and effective patient management. This study aims to develop a novel, explainable attention-based deep network to analyze radiomic patterns for predicting heterogeneous breast cancer types using ultrasound imaging. Materials and methods A multicentric retrospective dataset comprises brightness-mode ultrasound images of breast tissue collected across five different centers/databases. A total of 3256 images, having biopsy-proven 2068 benign and 1188 malignant lesions, were analyzed. A lightweight and computationally scalable network, WinDWS-SwinNet, is developed for binary and multipathology breast cancer classification. An optimized image preprocessing algorithm is proposed to enhance ultrasound radiomic features, thereby improving data generalizability and diagnostic accuracy. Results The WinDWS-SwinNet architecture demonstrated superior performance in breast cancer classification, achieving an area under the curve of 0.96, an overall test accuracy of 95.79%, and robust class-wise results with 95.11% precision and 98.51% sensitivity for benign tumors and 97.13% precision and 90.86% sensitivity for malignant tumors. For multipathology classification, the model achieved a test accuracy of 93%, with class-wise accuracies ranging from 94% to 99.5%. External validation on the independent unseen dataset resulted in an accuracy of 95.36%, highlighting the robustness and generalizability of the proposed model beyond the training data. Conclusion The developed methodology shows promising results in characterizing breast lesions into pathological subtypes noninvasively, effectively mimicking real-world diagnostic workflows, thereby supporting radiologists in reducing diagnostic uncertainty and enhancing confidence in clinical decision-making.

title: Incremental Prognostic Value of White Matter Hyperintensity Beyond Coronary Artery Disease Reporting and Data System for Major Adverse Cardiovascular Events.
abstract: Rationale and objectives This study aimed to assess the additional prognostic value of white matter hyperintensity (WMH) beyond Coronary Artery Disease Reporting and Data System (CAD-RADS) for major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) in patients with suspected or known coronary artery disease (CAD). Materials and methods This study included 1085 patients who underwent coronary computed tomography angiography and brain magnetic resonance imaging between November 2018 and December 2022. Time-dependent receiver operating characteristic curves were used to evaluate the predictive values, and the C-statistic was employed to determine their discriminatory power. Results 170 (15.7%) patients experienced MACE during a median follow-up of 63.1 months. WMH remained a significant and independent risk factor for predicting MACE after adjustments with clinical variables alone or with CAD-RADS. In the training set, the clinical-CAD-RADS-WMH model showed area under the curves (AUCs) of 0.719, 0.740, and 0.776 for predicting MACE at 1, 3, and 5 years, respectively. The model showed a consistent performance trend with AUCs of 0.819, 0.836, and 0.823 in the test set over 1, 3, and 5 years, respectively. Both the addition of WMH to the clinical model and to the clinical plus CAD-RADS model significantly increased the C-statistic index (p = 0.007, p = 0.038 in the training set and p = 0.002, p = 0.004 in the test set). These trends continued to be present when WMH was analyzed as a continuous variable. Conclusion An elevated WMH was related to a higher risk of MACE in patients with suspected or established CAD. Moreover, WMH demonstrated additional prognostic value for MACE beyond CAD-RADS.

title: MRI Interpretation of Suspected Pediatric Acute Appendicitis: The Role of Pediatric Subspecialty Training.
abstract: Rationale and objectives Magnetic resonance diagnosis of pediatric acute appendicitis is highly accurate but may vary depending on reader training and subspecialty expertise. The study aims to compare the diagnostic performance of fellowship-trained pediatric radiologists and nonpediatric fellowship-trained emergency radiologists for non-contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) diagnosis of suspected pediatric acute appendicitis (AA). Materials and methods Retrospective, single-center study including 122 patients who underwent non-contrast-enhanced MRI for clinical concern of AA, following equivocal or inconclusive ultrasound. Reference standard based on clinical follow-up and surgical notes. Two fellowship-trained pediatric radiologists and two nonpediatric fellowship-trained emergency radiologists independently reviewed the examinations using a standardized yes/no case report form. Paired comparisons used McNemar's test. Predictive values are reported descriptively with 95% confidence intervals, with between-groups differences assessed using case-level bootstrap resampling. Appendix visualization was analyzed descriptively only. Results The cohort included 122 patients (63 male [51.6%], 59 female [48.4%]; median age 11 years, IQR 7-13 years, range 4-18 years), of whom 31 (25.4%) had pathology-confirmed AA. Sensitivity for MRI diagnosis of AA was similar between groups (fellowship-trained pediatric 87.1% [71.1-94.9] vs nonpediatric fellowship-trained 90.3% [75.1-96.7]; P = 1.00), with higher specificity among pediatric radiologists (97.8% [92.3-99.4] vs 84.6% [75.8-90.6]; P = 0.002). Specificity was also higher among pediatric radiologists for direct signs (98.9% [94.0-99.8] vs 86.8% [78.4-92.3]; P = 0.001) and for combined direct and indirect signs (98.9% vs 92.3%; P = 0.03), as was accuracy for MRI diagnosis of AA (95.1% [89.7-97.7] vs 86.1% [78.8-91.1]; P = 0.03) and for direct signs (94.3% vs 86.1%; P = 0.03). Positive predictive value was higher among pediatric radiologists for the diagnosis of AA, direct signs, and combined direct and indirect signs, reaching 96.2% (81.1-99.3) vs 68.4% (52.5-80.9) for direct signs (P < 0.001). Negative predictive value did not differ in any category. Interpretation time was longer for pediatric radiologists, with a median paired difference of 23.5 seconds (P = 0.04). Conclusion Fellowship-trained pediatric radiologists had higher specificity, positive predictive value, and accuracy than non-pediatric emergency radiologists for MRI diagnosis of suspected pediatric AA, with a small difference in interpretation time (median, 24 seconds). These findings, based on a limited number of readers, suggest differences in subspecialty expertise and aims and support further multicenter evaluation.

title: Peritumoral Edema Outperforms Solid Tumor for Predicting TERTp Mutation in IDH Wild-Type Gliomas: A Multiparametric Diffusion MRI Histogram Study with Prognostic Analysis.
abstract: Rationale and objectives To investigate the preoperative predictive value of histogram features of diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI), diffusion kurtosis imaging (DKI), and intravoxel incoherent motion (IVIM) parameters for isocitrate dehydrogenase (IDH) and telomerase reverse transcriptase promoter (TERTp) mutation status in adult diffuse gliomas, and to identify independent prognostic factors for overall survival (OS). Materials and methods This retrospective study included 404 patients who underwent DWI, DKI, and IVIM imaging. Region-specific logistic regression models were developed using stratified 70:30 training and hold-out test splits. Logistic regression and receiver operating characteristic curves were used to assess predictive performance. Decision-curve, synthetic minority over-sampling technique (SMOTE) sensitivity, and bootstrap stability analyses were also performed. Prognostic factors were evaluated using Cox regression in 343 patients with follow-up. Results For IDH prediction, areas under the curve (AUCs) ranged from 0.874 to 0.920 in solid tumor and 0.902 to 0.936 in peritumoral edema, without significant between-region differences. For TERTp prediction in IDH wild-type gliomas, peritumoral edema models achieved higher AUCs than their solid tumor counterparts: DWI, 0.893 versus 0.677 (P = 0.019); DKI, 0.916 versus 0.754 (P = 0.036); IVIM, 0.934 versus 0.819 (P = 0.022); and combined, 0.948 versus 0.819 (P = 0.020). Decision-curve analysis favored the peritumoral edema combined model, and the regional discrimination pattern persisted after SMOTE balancing. In the overall cohort, peritumoral edema K skewness , D* 10th , and f entropy were independently associated with OS, alongside age, IDH status, O6-methylguanine-DNA methyltransferase promoter methylation, and Ki-67 LI. Within the IDH wild-type subgroup, age, TERTp status, and Ki-67 LI were independent prognostic factors. Conclusion Diffusion histogram models provided high discrimination for IDH status in both regions. Peritumoral edema models offered superior TERTp prediction in IDH wild-type gliomas, while selected peritumoral features provided prognostic information in the overall cohort.

title: Cooperative Poly(ethylene glycol) Dehydration and Ion-Dependent Electrostatic Interactions Drive Thermally Irreversible Polyion Complex Flower Micelle Hydrogels.
abstract: Thermoresponsive hydrogels based on flower-micelle assemblies that undergo gelation upon heating are attractive as injectable soft materials. We previously reported that Redox Injectable Gels (RIGs), formed from polyion complex (PIC) flower micelles, exhibit unusually high stiffness together with thermally irreversible gelation. Here, we investigate the physicochemical basis of this distinctive behavior by systematically examining the effects of phosphate buffer concentration and salt species on gelation dynamics, micellar structure, and segmental mobility. Rheological analyses showed that gelation accelerated with increasing buffer concentration, whereas the maximum storage modulus exhibited a nonmonotonic dependence, reaching a minimum at intermediate ionic conditions. Salt addition further modulated gel stiffness in an ion- and concentration-dependent manner, consistent with an ionic window in which moderate electrostatic screening alters electrostatic complexation within PIC cores and may facilitate micellar reorganization, whereas excessive screening at higher ionic strengths suppresses network reinforcement. Complementary dynamic light scattering (DLS), proton nuclear magnetic resonance ( 1 H NMR), fluorescence quenching, and pyrene solvatochromism collectively indicate that poly(ethylene glycol) (PEG) dehydration-consistent with cloud-point depression under high ionic strength-together with ion-dependent modulation of electrostatic interactions contributes to micelle reorganization and network formation. Collectively, these findings support a cooperative mechanistic framework in which PEG dehydration and ion-dependent modulation of electrostatic interactions jointly contribute to the robust and thermally irreversible gelation of RIGs. This framework provides design principles for tuning ionic environments to engineer mechanically robust thermoresponsive injectable hydrogels for biomedical applications under physiologically relevant ionic conditions. STATEMENT OF SIGNIFICANCE: Thermoresponsive injectable hydrogels are attractive biomaterials, but conventional flower-micelle systems typically exhibit weak mechanical properties and thermoreversible gelation. This study clarifies why redox injectable gels (RIGs), formed from polyion complex flower micelles, exhibit unusually high stiffness together with thermally irreversible gelation. By systematically varying buffer concentration and salt species, we show that gelation is strongly influenced by poly(ethylene glycol) (PEG) dehydration and ion-dependent modulation of electrostatic interactions within PIC micelles. These findings support a cooperative mechanistic framework for understanding salt- and buffer-dependent gelation and provide design principles for developing mechanically robust injectable biomaterials under physiologically relevant ionic environments.

title: Region-dependent in vivo degradation and local repair responses of a magnesium artificial lamina in a rabbit lamina defect model.
abstract: Magnesium (Mg)-based implants are promising for lamina defect reconstruction because of their biodegradability, mechanical compatibility, and bioactivity. However, in vivo degradation is usually assessed at the whole-implant level, and it remains unclear whether distinct regions of the same implant experience different degradation-repair couplings. In this study, a ZE21C Mg alloy artificial lamina was implanted in a New Zealand rabbit lumbar lamina defect reconstruction model to evaluate region-dependent degradation and local repair responses. Finite element analysis showed higher equivalent stress and strain on the residual-bone side. SEM/EDS and micro-CT analyses demonstrated the asymmetric degradation of the same implant in vivo. The residual-bone side exhibited faster Mg degradation, more severe surface and interfacial degradation, and higher TRAP-related remodeling activity, whereas the opposite side degraded more slowly, maintained a denser interface, and exhibited better bone formation and tissue integration. At 12 weeks, the remaining implant volume was 20.2 ± 2.0% on the residual-bone side, compared with 41.9 ± 5.3% on the opposite side, demonstrating pronounced region-dependent degradation within the same implant. Transcriptomic analysis indicated that rapid degradation was accompanied by stronger bone resorption and inflammatory interface reactions. The slow degradation area is associated with a more vascularized repair microenvironment that supports the matrix. These findings indicate that accelerated regional degradation does not necessarily promote bone regeneration. Therefore, region-specific degradation control may be critical for designing biodegradable Mg implants in complex anatomical environments. STATEMENT OF SIGNIFICANCE: Biodegradable magnesium implants are generally evaluated by their average degradation rate, despite regional differences in mechanical and biological environments. In a rabbit lamina reconstruction model, we directly compared two regions of the same ZE21C magnesium artificial lamina, limiting implant- and animal-level variability. The residual-bone side experienced higher stress, faster degradation, a less stable interface, stronger osteoclast-related activity, and poorer bone formation; the opposite side degraded more slowly and supported better tissue integration. Transcriptomic analysis linked these outcomes to distinct inflammatory, bone-resorptive, vascular, and matrix-remodeling responses. Thus, faster magnesium degradation does not necessarily improve repair. This work identifies region-specific degradation control as a key design principle for biodegradable orthopedic implants in complex anatomical environments.

title: A natural neuronal receptor-derived MRI probe targets β-amyloid oligomers for the diagnosis of Alzheimer's disease.
abstract: Early-to-mid detection of Alzheimer's disease (AD) remains challenging because clinically used amyloid positron emission tomography (PET) probes primarily visualize fibrillar β-amyloid (Aβ) deposits and require radioactive isotopes. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) offers a radiation-free alternative, but its application in molecular AD diagnosis is limited by insufficient blood-brain barrier (BBB) penetration and poor specificity toward early-to-mid Aβ species. Here, we developed a BBB-crossing liposomal MRI probe, Lipo@D1D2-Gd, by integrating a natural Aβ oligomer-binding receptor domain with a gadolinium chelator. The extracellular D1D2 domains of human leukocyte immunoglobulin-like receptor B2 (LilrB2), a neuronal receptor that recognizes neurotoxic Aβ oligomers, were recombinantly produced and bioorthogonally conjugated with a gadolinium chelator. The resulting D1D2-Gd retained its Aβ-binding capability and MRI contrast activity. To enable brain delivery, D1D2-Gd was encapsulated within maltose-functionalized PEGylated liposomes designed to facilitate BBB transport. After intravenous administration to 4-month-old 5xFAD mice, Lipo@D1D2-Gd crossed the BBB, accumulated in Aβ-rich brain regions, and generated MRI contrast enhancement that differentiated 5xFAD mice from wild-type controls. Systemic safety evaluation showed no obvious hematological, biochemical, or histological toxicity. This study establishes a receptor-derived, BBB-crossing biomaterial platform for radiation-free molecular imaging of early-to-mid AD-associated Aβ pathology. STATEMENT OF SIGNIFICANCE: 1) Promising Targeting Strategy: We repurposed a human-derived natural receptor domain (LilrB2 D1D2) as a targeting module for β-amyloid (Aβ) oligomers, a key pathogenic species in Alzheimer's disease (AD). 2) Non-invasive MRI Approach: We constructed a liposomal probe designed to deliver the Gd-labeled targeting agent to the brain, enabling the detection of Aβ-associated pathology in 4-month-old 5xFAD mice via non-radioactive MRI, well before overt cognitive decline. 3) Experimental Validation: We demonstrate the probe's association with Aβ oligomers/plaques, effective BBB crossing, differences in MRI signals between AD model and wild-type mice, and an initially favorable biosafety profile, with no observed toxicity under the tested conditions. 4) Clinical Translation Potential: Our work presents a promising pathway toward a safe, accessible, and early-to-mid-stage AD screening tool, with the potential to facilitate population-wide screening and earlier therapeutic intervention.

title: The diagnostic utility of abdominal and bowel ultrasound in detecting gastrointestinal and hepatic manifestations of rheumatoid arthritis.
abstract: Background and study aims Patients with Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) may develop digestive and hepatic complications. Abdominal ultrasound is sensitive to assess bowel abnormalities. We aimed to evaluate the frequency of gastrointestinal (GI) and hepatic disorders in RA patients and study the reliability of abdominal ultrasound in detecting these disorders to allow early management and better prognosis. Patients and methods 70 RA patients and 70 non-RA people as a reference control group were included in this study. Both study groups were subjected to the Rome IV criteria, the gastroesophageal reflux disease questionnaire, and trans-abdominal ultrasound. Transient elastography was done for subjects with bright or bright coarse liver on ultrasound. Results Irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) and Gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) were statistically significantly higher in RA patients (28.5% and 51.4% respectively) than in the non-RA group (11.4% and 12.8% respectively) (p value = 0.019 and 0.000 respectively). Bright or bright coarse liver was statistically significantly higher in RA patients than in the non-RA group (p value = 0.000) and was statistically significantly higher in RA patients on methotrexate-based therapy (p value = 0.012). Only 2 RA patients (5.4%) had significant fibrosis (≥F2). Conclusion Abdominal ultrasound is recommended in the routine evaluation of the liver besides liver enzymes while bowel ultrasound is not recommended as routine screening in RA patients in the absence of complaint.

title: Interpretable Machine Learning for Course Prediction in Central Serous Chorioretinopathy Using Baseline OCT from a Multicenter Cohort.
abstract: Purpose To predict disease clinical course in central serous chorioretinopathy (CSC) using an interpretable machine learning model applied to baseline artificial intelligence (AI)-derived optical coherence tomography (OCT) biomarkers acquired at first presentation. Design Multicenter, retrospective cohort study. Participants Overall, 329 treatment-naïve CSC eyes recruited across eight international centers in Europe, the Middle East, Asia, and North Africa. Methods Treatment-naïve CSC patients were retrospectively included and classified, based on follow-up, as acute or chronic CSC according to subretinal fluid (SRF) resolution. Baseline OCT biomarkers were extracted using an AI-based platform (Discovery OCT Biomarker Detector; RetinAI AG, Switzerland), which quantified retinal layer thicknesses, including the outer nuclear layer (ONL) and photoreceptor-retinal pigment epithelium (PR+RPE) complex, fluid volumes (SRF and RPE detachment [PED]), and biomarker probabilities, across central, parafoveal, and perifoveal ETDRS regions. These features used to develop an interpretable machine learning model predicting future CSC chronicity. Main outcome measures Classification of eyes as acute or chronic CSC, determined by SRF resolution on follow-up; discriminative performance of the Random Forest classifier, assessed by area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC); and biomarker importance, evaluated using SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) values. Results Of 329 eyes (291 patients), 92 (28.0%) were classified as acute and 237 (72.0%) as chronic CSC; mean follow-up was 4.2 ± 1.6 years. Chronic CSC patients were significantly older (51.7 ± 12.6 vs. 43.2 ± 9.6 years, p<0.001) with worse baseline visual acuity (0.25 ± 0.21 vs. 0.16 ± 0.15 logMAR, p=0.029). Among baseline OCT biomarkers, parafoveal ONL thickness showed the strongest association with disease chronicity (q<0.0001; r=-0.414). The Random Forest classifier achieved an AUC of 0.852 (95% CI: 0.748-0.940). SHAP analysis identified parafoveal ONL thickness, perifoveal PR+RPE thickness, and central SRF volume as the strongest predictors of acute CSC, whereas greater RNFL thickness, PED volume, FLAT PED probability, and HF probability were the most influential predictors of chronic disease. Conclusions Automatically detected OCT biomarkers can predict CSC chronicity at initial presentation with good discriminatory performance. Quantitative markers of outer retinal integrity, fluid configuration, and RPE dysfunction may improve prognostication, facilitate patient counseling, and help identify individuals at increased risk of persistent CSC.

title: Ocular Metastasis: Clinical Course and Survival Analysis of 569 Patients (727 Eyes) Over a 40-Year Interval (1979-2018).
abstract: Objective To report the clinical course of a large series of patients with intraocular and epibulbar metastases to the eye encountered over a 40-year interval and determine whether recent systemic treatments have improved patient survival following detection compared to earlier cases. Design Retrospective case series and trend study. Subjects 727 eyes of 569 patients diagnosed with metastasis to the eye(s). Methods Retrospective chart review and statistical analysis with SPSS (including descriptive statistics, cross-tabulations, statistical comparison of distributions, actuarial event rate curves using both Kaplan-Meier and life table methods, and comparison of survival curves using the log rank test). Main outcome measures Sex and age of patients, source cancer and metastatic history, symptoms, laterality and focality of eye metastases, ocular sites of involvement, largest basal diameter and thickness of metastases, ocular biopsies, systemic and ophthalmic treatment, symptomatic and tumor response to treatment, cause of death, and median, 5-year, 10-year, and comparative overall survival among various categorical subgroups. Results We identified dates of death for 98.1% of 569 patients. The median overall survival was 8.2 months, the 5-year overall survival was 8.2%, and the 10-year overall survival was 2.8%. Patients encountered in the second half of the study interval did not have significantly better survival compared to those in the first half. Breast cancer was the most common primary cancer. Lung cancer follows as the second most common primary, with affected patients having far worse survival outcomes. Treatment was administered in 435 worse or only affected eyes, and of the 313 of those for which we have follow-up visual acuity data, visual acuity improved or remained stable in 62.6%. Of the 286 of those for which we have a follow-up fundus examination, 85.7% demonstrated initial complete or partial regression. One hundred fifty-seven of 569 total patients (27.6%) ultimately had bilateral ocular involvement. Conclusions Survival for patients with cancer metastatic to the eye, which remains extremely poor, did not improve significantly from 1979 to 2018. Breast and lung cancer remain the predominant primary cancers and are followed by gastrointestinal, hematologic, and genitourinary cancers. Based on available but incomplete data, treatment improves or maintains vision and shrinks metastases in most patients.

title: Pediatric Endothelial Keratoplasty: A Modified Delphi Consensus by the EKLG Study Group on Indications, Surgical Techniques, and Postoperative Care.
abstract: Purpose To identify areas of consensus among global experts on the clinical management of pediatric endothelial keratoplasty (EK), including patient selection, timing, preoperative evaluation, technique selection, intraoperative standards, and postoperative care, and to provide a practical framework for surgeons earlier in their pediatric EK learning curve. Design Modified Delphi-based global consensus study. Participants International ophthalmologists with expertise in endothelial keratoplasty and pediatric corneal diseases. Methods A series of consensus statements on pediatric EK were developed from iterative rounds of structured questions and statements posed to a panel of experts. Two rounds of asynchronous electronic questionnaires were followed by a structured hybrid discussion of unresolved items. Experts responded anonymously to statements assessing consensus and to revised items addressing indications, contraindications, timing, preoperative workup, technique selection, intraoperative standards, and postoperative management. Results are reported using item-specific denominators because occasional non-response occurred across the survey items. Main outcome measures Consensus was defined as ≥70% agreement among the experts. Agreement between 60% and 69.9% was considered to be near consensus. Results The consensus supported pediatric EK for congenital hereditary endothelial dystrophy, aphakic or pseudophakic corneal edema, persistent corneal edema in congenital glaucoma, X-linked endothelial corneal dystrophy, iatrogenic endothelial decompensation, and trauma-related decompensation. EK was inappropriate for severe anterior segment dysgenesis with keratolenticular or extensive iridocorneal adhesions. In Round 2, experts further endorsed EK for failed penetrating keratoplasty due to endothelial failure, congenital glaucoma with visually significant Haab's striae, and forceps injury involving the visual axis. There was a consensus that the timing of intervention should be guided primarily by amblyopia risk rather than by a specific age cut off. Essential preoperative assessments included examination under anesthesia, B-scan ultrasonography, anterior segment optical coherence tomography, intraocular pressure measurement, ultrasound biomicroscopy, and refraction. Experts agreed that ultrathin-DSAEK and DSAEK are the predominant techniques, whereas DMEK is currently selectively reserved, usually for older children with uncomplicated anterior segment anatomy. Preferred intraoperative principles included air tamponade, anterior chamber maintenance, and donor graft under-sizing relative to the corneal diameter. Postoperative recommendations included early intraocular pressure assessment, topical corticosteroid therapy for > 6 months, regular monitoring for steroid response, selective contact lens use, and individualized long-term follow-up. Conclusions The consensus statements provide globally endorsed recommendations for the clinical management of pediatric EK. These guidelines are relevant for corneal specialists providing a practical framework to benchmark practice, reduce variability, and guide future multicenter investigations.

The consensus supported pediatric EK for congenital hereditary endothelial dystrophy, aphakic or pseudophakic corneal edema, persistent corneal edema in congenital glaucoma, X-linked endothelial corneal dystrophy, iatrogenic endothelial decompensation, and trauma-related decompensation. EK was inappropriate for severe anterior segment dysgenesis with keratolenticular or extensive iridocorneal adhesions. In Round 2, experts further endorsed EK for failed penetrating keratoplasty due to endothelial failure, congenital glaucoma with visually significant Haab's striae, and forceps injury involving the visual axis. There was a consensus that the timing of intervention should be guided primarily by amblyopia risk rather than by a specific age cut off. Essential preoperative assessments included examination under anesthesia, B-scan ultrasonography, anterior segment optical coherence tomography, intraocular pressure measurement, ultrasound biomicroscopy, and refraction. Experts agreed that ultrathin-DSAEK and DSAEK are the predominant techniques, whereas DMEK is currently selectively reserved, usually for older children with uncomplicated anterior segment anatomy. Preferred intraoperative principles included air tamponade, anterior chamber maintenance, and donor graft under-sizing relative to the corneal diameter. Postoperative recommendations included early intraocular pressure assessment, topical corticosteroid therapy for > 6 months, regular monitoring for steroid response, selective contact lens use, and individualized long-term follow-up.

Conclusions

The consensus statements provide globally endorsed recommendations for the clinical management of pediatric EK. These guidelines are relevant for corneal specialists providing a practical framework to benchmark practice, reduce variability, and guide future multicenter investigations.

title: Three-dimensional analysis of maxillary alveolar bone and point A remodeling after premolar-extraction decompensation in patients with skeletal Class III malocclusion.
abstract: Introduction This study evaluated the remodeling patterns of point A (subspinale) and the maxillary alveolar bone after premolar-extraction decompensation in patients with skeletal Class III malocclusion. Methods Cone-beam computed tomography data from 40 patients with skeletal Class III malocclusion were collected before and after presurgical decompensation (pre-DC and post-DC). A 3-dimensional cephalometric analysis was used to evaluate dentoskeletal changes. Surface-based registration and voxel-based analysis were used to assess anterior maxillary displacement. The root length, alveolar bone height, and thickness were measured for the maxillary anterior teeth. Pearson correlation was used to analyze the associations between point A and other parameters. Results SNA, FH-NA, U1-SN, and U1-NA decreased by 1.22°, 0.99°, 9.43°, and 7.06° (P < 0.001). All landmarks moved posteriorly (P < 0.001): point A by 1.07 mm, superior prosthion by 3.87 mm, maxillary central incisor incisal midpoint by 5.28 mm, and root apex by 2.26 mm. Bodily movement of the anterior teeth accounted for an average of 41% of the retraction, and tipping accounted for 59%. Point A retraction was weakly positively correlated with SNA (r = 0.336), FH-NA (r = 0.312), and the proportion of bodily retraction (r = 0.288) and weakly negatively correlated with U1-SN (r = -0.306), U1-NA (r = -0.354), and the proportion of tipping retraction (r = -0.288). However, Bonferroni correction substantially reduced the significance of these correlations. The maxillary anterior teeth showed partial root resorption (mean, 1.11-1.97 mm); the palatal alveolar bone thinned significantly in the cervical and middle thirds, whereas labial bone volume increased apically. Conclusions Decompensation typically displaces maxillary teeth, alveolar bone, and point A posteriorly in patients with skeletal Class III malocclusion, frequently accompanied by palatal alveolar bone resorption. Hard-soft tissue remodeling resulting from changes in tooth position and point A should be incorporated into initial treatment planning to individualize the mode and amount of maxillary incisor retraction, which is critical for patients with Class III malocclusion who are ineligible for bimaxillary surgery or who require only mandibular surgery.

title: Mandibular symphysis morphology and mandibular incisor inclination across skeletal patterns: A 3-dimensional cone-beam computed tomography analysis.
abstract: Introduction This cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) study evaluated the association between mandibular symphyseal morphology and incisor inclination across diverse sagittal and vertical skeletal patterns. Methods CBCT scans of 108 adults were retrospectively analyzed. Subjects were classified into sagittal patterns based on the Wits appraisal and into vertical patterns according to the maxillomandibular plane angle. Linear and angular symphyseal parameters were measured along the long axis of the most anterior mandibular incisor. Relationships between these parameters and mandibular incisor inclination (IMPA) were evaluated using 1-way analysis of variance, Pearson correlation, and intraclass correlation coefficients for reliability. Results Vertical patterns showed significant variation, whereas sagittal groups did not. Patients with hyperdivergence exhibited larger symphyseal ratios and narrower apical widths (P <0.01). IMPA correlated positively with symphyseal angle and apical width (P <0.001). A sagittal Class II relationship predicted increased IMPA (P <0.001), with no significant sagittal-by-vertical interactions (P >0.05). Conclusions Mandibular symphysis morphology is primarily influenced by vertical skeletal patterns and incisor inclination, acting largely independently of sagittal variations. These findings emphasize the importance of CBCT-based individualized assessment in orthodontic diagnosis and treatment planning.

title: Association Between Cardiac Computed Tomography-Detected Patent Foramen Ovale and Risk of Ischemic Stroke.
abstract: Patent foramen ovale (PFO) is associated with embolic stroke; however, the prognostic significance of PFO detected by cardiac computed tomography (CT) remains unclear. Objectives: This study aimed to evaluate the association between CT-detected PFO and subsequent ischemic stroke risk, and to assess its agreement with transthoracic echocardiography with agitated saline (Bubble-TTE). We retrospectively analyzed 1,028 patients who underwent cardiac CT between 2016 and 2018. PFO was diagnosed on cardiac CT using criteria adapted from previous reports. In a subset of 86 patients, intermodality agreement between cardiac CT and Bubble-TTE was assessed. The primary outcome was ischemic stroke, and the secondary outcome was all-cause mortality. CT-detected PFO was identified in 212 patients (20.6%). In the subset analysis, cardiac CT showed moderate agreement with Bubble-TTE for PFO detection (κ = 0.41, p < 0.001). During follow-up, ischemic stroke occurred in 49 patients (4.7%), and 116 patients died (11.3%). CT-detected PFO was independently associated with ischemic stroke (adjusted hazard ratio 2.41, 95% confidence interval 1.36-4.29, p = 0.003), whereas no significant association was observed with all-cause mortality (adjusted hazard ratio 0.96, 95% confidence interval 0.61-1.50, p = 0.86). In conclusion, CT-detected PFO was associated with an increased risk of ischemic stroke but not with all-cause mortality, suggesting prognostic relevance for ischemic stroke.

title: Outcomes and complications of parathyroidectomy in otorhinolaryngology practice: A single-institution, 10-year retrospective observational study.
abstract: Background Parathyroidectomy is associated with a spectrum of potential complications, including recurrent laryngeal nerve (RLN) injury, permanent hypocalcemia, postoperative hemorrhage, wound infection, and recurrence of hyperparathyroidism (HPT). The objective of this study was to evaluate the outcomes of 223 parathyroid procedures and to determine the incidence of procedure-related complications. Methods This retrospective observational study analyzed parathyroidectomy cases performed between 2013 and 2022. Demographic data and postoperative complications were collected and assessed. The success rates of surgical removal of parathyroid adenomas, hyperplasia, carcinomas, and cysts were evaluated in relation to preoperative and perioperative diagnostic methods. Results A total of 223 parathyroidectomy procedures were performed. Unilateral permanent RLN palsy was observed in 0.91% of cases (95% CI, 0.11-3.21%). Bilateral permanent vocal cord palsy was not observed. A positive response to the parathyroidectomy was observed in 98.43% (95% CI, 96.1-99.72%). Temporary hypercalcemia developed in 13.26% (95% CI, 9.41-18.35%). Revision surgery for persistent HPT or recurrence of HPT was necessary in 16 cases. Conclusion The combination of preoperative multimodal imaging and precise hyperparathyroidism diagnosis is essential for reducing the risk of unsuccessful localization in parathyroid surgery. Ultrasound and scintigraphy offers the most effective diagnostic method. Intraoperative neuromonitoring is recommended for revision surgeries.

title: Expert assessment of medical and organizational care for children with congenital ear malformations in the Republic of Kazakhstan: The RAND/UCLA appropriateness method.
abstract: Congenital auditory anomalies are serious conditions ranging from mild hearing loss to complete deafness, with associated speech impairment, social limitations, and disability. Our aim was to evaluate the appropriateness of medical and organizational care interventions for children with congenital ear malformations (microtia and aural atresia) in the Republic of Kazakhstan, using the RAND/UCLA Appropriateness Method. Methods A nine-member multidisciplinary expert panel (otorhinolaryngologists, audiologists, pediatricians, and otologic surgeons) rated 93 diagnostic, therapeutic, and rehabilitation interventions using a structured 9-point appropriateness scale across two rounds of evaluation. Consensus was defined as a numerical IQR (Q3-Q1) ≤2 score points combined with ≥75% of ratings within the same category. Appropriateness categories were defined as: Appropriate (median 7-9), Uncertain (4-6), and Inappropriate (1-3). Results Of 93 rated interventions, 43 (46%) reached consensus as Appropriate, 45 (48%) were classified as Uncertain, and 5 (5%) as Inappropriate. Highest appropriateness was assigned to multidisciplinary diagnostic consultations (ENT specialist, audiologist, otologic surgeon) and imaging (high-resolution CT of the temporal bones, MRI). For bilateral aural atresia, bone conduction devices were rated as Appropriate (mean 7.55-7.66). Non-intervention approaches received the lowest ratings (mean 1.11-3.00), indicating strong expert consensus against expectant management. Key organizational barriers were included as explicitly rated items in the questionnaire (items 85-93, Section 4-5 of Appendix A). Delayed or absent patient registration and follow-up (item 86, mean 8.00, median 8, Appropriate) and inadequacies in regulatory frameworks (item 87, mean 7.22, median 7, Appropriate†) were among the highest-rated organizational items, while insufficient funding (item 88, mean 6.22, median 6, Uncertain without consensus) did not reach consensus. Conclusion This first application of the RAND/UCLA method in Kazakhstan to evaluate care for children with congenital ear malformations identified clear areas of expert consensus and uncertainty. The results support the development of multidisciplinary care pathways and targeted rehabilitation policies. Findings represent structured expert opinion from nine specialist panelists in Kazakhstan and should not be interpreted as evidence of clinical effectiveness, cost-effectiveness, or national representativeness.

title: Technical optimization in adenotonsillar surgery: A practical narrative review of strategies to improve surgical exposure, safety, and visualization.
abstract: Objective To critically synthesize and integrate intraoperative technical strategies designed to optimize visualization, surgical exposure, tissue protection, and/or hemostatic control during adenotonsillar surgery. Methods A structured narrative review was conducted using PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, ScienceDirect, and the Cochrane Library to identify studies published between January 1996 and May 2026. The search strategy combined MeSH terms and free-text keywords related to adenotonsillectomy, operative visualization, surgical exposure, hemostasis, tissue protection, microscopy, endoscopy, and suction-assisted techniques. Following title and abstract screening and full-text assessment, 38 studies were included in the final qualitative synthesis. Results The available evidence indicates that multiple complementary intraoperative strategies can improve operative precision and surgical safety during adenotonsillar surgery. Microscope- and endoscope-assisted techniques enhance anatomical visualization, facilitate targeted hemostasis, and improve the identification of residual lymphoid tissue and occult bleeding sites. Cheek expanders and modified retraction systems increase transverse surgical exposure and improve instrument maneuverability. Protective measures, including salivary cotton rolls and moist gauze, may reduce pressure- and thermal-related mucosal injury involving the oral commissures, uvula, and posterior pharyngeal wall. Mirror-assisted visualization and soft palate retraction using a Nelaton catheter optimize nasopharyngeal inspection during adenoidectomy. Additional hemostatic measures, including topical vasoconstrictors, gauze packing, warm saline irrigation, continuous suction, and suction coagulation, may reduce intraoperative bleeding while minimizing unnecessary thermal injury. Conclusions Optimizing adenotonsillar surgery extends beyond the choice of surgical device. Simple, inexpensive, and reproducible technical modifications can substantially improve visualization, surgical exposure, hemostatic control, tissue preservation, and operative ergonomics, thereby contributing to safer, more standardized, and potentially more effective surgical procedures.

title: Capivasertib plus abiraterone in PTEN-deficient de novo metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer: updated survival analysis from CAPItello-281.
abstract: Background Patients with phosphatase and tensin homolog (PTEN)-deficient de novo metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer (mHSPC) have poor prognosis and reduced benefit from current standard of care. The phase III CAPItello-281 study (NCT04493853) showed a statistically significant benefit in radiographic progression-free survival (rPFS) with capivasertib plus abiraterone versus placebo plus abiraterone (combined with prednisone/prednisolone and androgen deprivation therapy): hazard ratio (HR) 0.81, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.66-0.98; P = 0.034. The HR for interim overall survival (OS; 26% maturity) was 0.90, 95% CI 0.71-1.15. Here, we report ad hoc, descriptive analyses at 42% OS data maturity. Patients and methods Patients with de novo mHSPC and PTEN-deficient tumors (defined as ≥90% of viable malignant cells with no specific cytoplasmic staining by immunohistochemistry) received capivasertib plus abiraterone or matched placebo (randomly assigned 1 : 1) plus abiraterone. Analyses carried out at this ad hoc data cut-off, including the alpha-controlled key secondary endpoint of OS as well as the primary endpoint of investigator-assessed rPFS, were descriptive and not prespecified in the protocol. Results A total of 1012 patients received capivasertib plus abiraterone (n = 507) or placebo plus abiraterone (n = 505). At this ad hoc analysis at 42% OS maturity (data cut-off: 9 March 2026), with 17 months' additional follow-up (median follow-up 39 months in both arms), HR for OS favored capivasertib plus abiraterone versus placebo plus abiraterone (HR 0.82, 95% CI 0.68-0.99, P = 0.044) and OS medians were reached: 57.4 versus 46.5 months. Updated rPFS (HR 0.83, 95% CI 0.70-0.99, nominal P = 0.033; median 35.5 versus 26.0 months) was consistent with the primary analysis. The safety profile remained consistent with the primary findings. Patients with de novo mHSPC and PTEN-deficient tumors (defined as ≥90% of viable malignant cells with no specific cytoplasmic staining by immunohistochemistry) received capivasertib plus abiraterone or matched placebo (randomly assigned 1 : 1) plus abiraterone. Analyses carried out at this ad hoc data cut-off, including the alpha-controlled key secondary endpoint of OS as well as the primary endpoint of investigator-assessed rPFS, were descriptive and not prespecified in the protocol.

A total of 1012 patients received capivasertib plus abiraterone (n = 507) or placebo plus abiraterone (n = 505). The safety profile remained consistent with the primary findings.

With longer follow-up, findings from this updated descriptive analysis support the clinically meaningful OS benefit of adding capivasertib to abiraterone in the treatment of patients with PTEN-deficient mHSPC. title: [Imaging of pulmonary nodules: A diagnostic approach].
abstract: The detection of pulmonary nodules has increased considerably with the widespread use of chest-computed tomography and the development of low-dose CT lung cancer screening. The pulmonary nodule represents a major diagnostic challenge, requiring rigorous evaluation in order to distinguish benign from malignant lesions while limiting unnecessary invasive investigations. Analysis relies on precise morphological characterization (density, size, margins), assessment of persistence and growth over time, and integration of the clinical context. The Fleischner Society guidelines and the protocols derived from organized screening programs now form the basis of standardized management. This article provides a detailed review of the radiological criteria, decision-making algorithms, and the role of transthoracic needle biopsy in the management of pulmonary nodules.

title: Tension pneumocephalus associated with nasopharyngeal carcinoma: A case report and literature review.
abstract: Background Nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) is commonly treated with radiotherapy and chemotherapy, particularly in advanced disease. Pneumocephalus is a rare complication of NPC and may become life-threatening when intracranial air accumulates under tension. Case presentation We report a 42-year-old man with recurrent NPC involving the skull base after prior chemotherapy and two courses of radiotherapy, with a cumulative radiation dose of 120Gy. He presented with headache, dizziness, confusion, vomiting, and right eye ptosis. Imaging demonstrated extensive pneumocephalus involving the ventricular system and basal cisterns, and CT cisternography showed skull-base fistulization in the setting of recurrent tumor. He was initially managed conservatively, but later developed acute neurological deterioration with bradycardia and CT findings consistent with tension pneumocephalus. Emergent external ventricular drain placement with aspiration of 120mL of air resulted in neurological recovery, and he was discharged home. Conclusion Tension pneumocephalus is a rare but serious complication that may occur in patients with recurrent NPC and skull-base involvement. Progressive tumor invasion/fistulization was the most directly supported mechanism in this case, while prior high-dose radiotherapy and suspected osteoradionecrosis may have contributed to skull-base fragility. Prompt imaging and multidisciplinary management are essential when selected NPC patients with skull-base disease develop new neurological symptoms.

title: Endoscopy timing in managing acute esophagogastric variceal bleeding: a multicenter retrospective study.
abstract: Background Patients suffering from acute esophagogastric variceal bleeding (AEGVB) frequently face unfavorable prognoses. Although endoscopy is the preferred intervention for AEGVB, the optimal timing for its administration to enhance patient outcomes remains a subject of ongoing debate. Methods This study encompassed patients with cirrhosis who presented with AEGVB and received endoscopic treatment at three major tertiary hospitals in Shandong Province, China, from January 2017 to July 2024. Participants were stratified based on the time interval from hospital admission to endoscopic intervention (<12 h vs. ≥12 h; <24 h vs. ≥24 h; <48 h vs. ≥48 h; <72 h vs. ≥72 h). Propensity score matching (PSM) was utilized in a 1:1 ratio for each group. Subgroup analyses were performed based on patients' hematemesis status, Child-Pugh classification, and Model for End-Stage Liver Disease (MELD) score. The primary outcomes assessed included overall post-endoscopic rebleeding, 5-day rebleeding, 6-week rebleeding, rebleeding beyond 180 days, in-hospital mortality, and 6-week mortality. Furthermore, a multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression model was employed to identify risk factors for rebleeding. Results Overall, 1125 patients who underwent endoscopic intervention for AEGVB were included. Prior to PSM, the group undergoing endoscopy within 12 h exhibited a significantly higher in-hospital mortality rate compared to the group undergoing endoscopy after 12 h (3.3%vs. 0.5%, P = 0.010). Post-PSM analysis revealed no significant differences between the two groups regarding in-hospital and 6-week mortality, overall post-endoscopic rebleeding, 5-day rebleeding, 6-week rebleeding, and rebleeding occurring beyond 180 days. In a subgroup analysis of patients presenting with hematemesis, those in the <24-hour group demonstrated a significantly higher incidence of overall post-endoscopic rebleeding (50.4%vs. 37.9%, P = 0.015) and rebleeding beyond 180 days post-treatment (29.9%vs. 19.3%, P = 0.014) compared to the ≥24 h group. Additionally, in the subgroup analysis of patients classified as Child-Pugh class B, the <24-hour group showed a significantly elevated rate of overall post-endoscopic rebleeding compared to the ≥24-hour group (50.0%vs. 38.2%, P = 0.026). This rate was also significantly higher in the <72-hour group compared to the ≥72-hour group (44.8%vs. 35.1%, P = 0.018). Notably, the incidence of rebleeding beyond 180 days post-endoscopic therapy was higher in the <72-hour group compared to the ≥72-hour group (25.2%vs. 17.7%, P = 0.029). Multivariate Cox regression analysis indicated that the timing of endoscopic therapy was not an independent risk factor for rebleeding. Conclusions In conclusion, for patients with AEGVB who can tolerate endoscopy, early endoscopic intervention may not enhance the overall prognosis.

title: International consensuses and guidelines on etiology, diagnosis, and treatment of retinal vein occlusion (RVO) by the Academy of Asia-Pacific Professors of Ophthalmology (AAPPO), Asia-Pacific Vitreo-retina Society (APVRS) and Academia Retina Internationalis (ARI).
abstract: Retinal vein occlusion (RVO) is a prevalent potentially blinding retinal vascular disease, with secondary macular edema, retinal ischemia, and ocular neovascular complications posing substantial threats to visual function. Supported by members of the Academy of Asia-Pacific Professors of Ophthalmology (AAPPO), Asia-Pacific Vitreo-retina Society (APVRS) and Academia Retina Internationalis (ARI), a consensus and guideline is provided a comprehensive update on the etiology, diagnosis and management of RVO. An updated consensus was judged necessary following numerous recent results from epidemiology studies, evolution of advanced imaging technologies and novel pharmacotherapeutics from clinical trials, including an expanding portfolio of anti-vascular endothelial growth factor (anti-VEGF) agents, drug delivery systems, and emerging evidence on relevant artificial intelligence. The formulation of these consensus statements were based on the review and discussion of a systematic search for the latest evidence-based data and voting by an International Panel of Experts (IPE) in the following key areas: I) Diagnostic controversies around classification systems and imaging modalities; II) Treatment controversies regarding anti-VEGF therapy, corticosteroid treatments, laser therapy, and surgical interventions; III) Management paradigm between standardized protocols from clinical trials and individualized approaches and IV) Emerging controversies in novel therapeutics. The primary goal was to furnish ophthalmologists with standardized, yet individualized, management protocols to try to optimize treatment safety and efficacy, ensuring alignment with contemporary clinical practices in the Asia-Pacific region.

title: Integrating deep learning and radiomics for accurate differentiation of benign and malignant breast microcalcifications on intraoperative specimen mammography.
abstract: Background Mammography (MG) remains the cornerstone imaging modality for early breast cancer screening, playing a pivotal role in lowering disease-specific mortality. Nevertheless, its diagnostic utility is constrained by a substantial false-negative rate, documented between 10% and 30%. This limitation poses significant clinical challenges in evaluating suspicious microcalcifications on surgical excision biopsy. Intraoperative frozen section analysis often yields inconclusive findings for such calcified lesions, potentially necessitating re-operation. Consequently, rigorous assessment of mammographic features in excised specimens is essential for optimizing surgical decision-making, particularly regarding the necessity and timing of intraoperative pathological evaluation. Methods This investigation involved a retrospective evaluation of 400 intraoperative specimen mammography obtained from individuals confirmed to have breast cancer at the Guangdong Provincial Hospital of Traditional Chinese Medicine. We herein focus exclusively on intraoperative specimen mammography, which is distinct from conventional screening mammography. Upon securing necessary ethical clearance, we assembled a rigorously screened dataset comprising 197 benign and 203 malignant instances. Prior to analysis, images were subjected to preprocessing steps such as grayscale transformation and histogram equalization to optimize them for deep learning ingestion. We subsequently constructed the EfficientNet_radiomics framework by fusing latent representations from the EfficientNet-B0 architecture with manually engineered radiomic descriptors extracted from the imaging data, a strategy designed to augment the system's diagnostic precision. Results Compared with conventional machine learning approaches and experienced radiologists, our framework yielded superior diagnostic metrics. Notably, it achieved 78.0% ± 7.0 accuracy in identifying benign calcifications versus 71.4% ± 8.0 for radiologists, and 83.0% ± 6.0 versus 81.8% ± 6.0 for malignant lesions, underscoring its translational value for clinical deployment. Conclusion The study holds promise as a real-time decision-support tool during intraoperative specimen evaluation, potentially reducing unnecessary frozen section analyses and re-operation rates by providing more accurate intraoperative differentiation, particularly for benign calcifications.

title: Validation of a 3D-printed anthropomorphic eye phantom for quality assurance in external beam radiotherapy using TLD and radiochromic film.
abstract: External beam radiation therapy (EBRT) is widely used for uveal melanoma to preserve the eye and achieve effective tumor control. However, late side effects remain a concern, reinforcing the need for dose reduction to mitigate long-term toxicity. This study aims to validate a 3D-printed ocular tissue-equivalent anthropomorphic phantom, with enhanced anatomical accuracy based on the Alderson Radiation Therapy Phantom, through end-to-end dosimetric analysis using radiochromic film and thermoluminescent dosimeters (TLDs) for research and quality assurance (QA) applications in EBRT. Gafchromic EBT3 films and LiF:Mg,Ti microcube TLDs were used for dose assessment in target volume and organs at risk (OAR). Calibration and irradiation were performed using a Varian Clinac iX and a TrueBeam linear accelerator with a 6 MV photon beam. Film dosimetry, with films positioned in axial and oblique planes, was processed using the Film2Dose software and compared to the Varian Eclipse® treatment planning system (TPS) via gamma analysis. For TLD analysis, lower limit of detection verification, reproducibility tests, individual calibration, and cone beam computed tomography (CBCT) dosimetry were made prior to the treatment dosimetry to ensure accuracy. For treatment dosimetry, TLD samples were placed in regions of interest (i.e. lens, eye fundus, PTV, and optic nerve) for point dose verification and compatibility analysis against the TPS. In the film analysis, maximum dose uncertainties of up to 16% were observed in low-dose regions (<10% of prescribed dose). Gamma analysis yielded a mean passing rate of 100% for 2%/2 mm/10% threshold criterion. All TLDdose measurements demonstrate statistical compatibility with TPS predictions using Z-score-based compatibility analysis. Uncertainties below 5% were found in experimental measurements and TPS point dose assessment. These results indicate the robustness of the dosimetric methods employed and support the validation of the developed 3D-printed, tissue-equivalent anthropomorphic ocular phantom for research and quality assurance applications in EBRT.

title: Enhanced two-stage cascaded network for high-precision stopping power ratio and functional image generation from conventional CT.
abstract: Purpose Accurate stopping power ratio (SPR) estimation is essential for proton therapy dose calculation; however, SPR and related functional images-electron density (ED), effective atomic number (Zeff), and iodine concentration (IC)-currently require dual-energy CT (DECT), whose clinical adoption is limited by high cost and restricted availability. To our knowledge, no previous study has synthesized DECT-derived functional images directly from conventional single-energy CT (SECT). This study proposes, for the first time, a deep learning framework that generates SPR, ED, Zeff, and IC maps simultaneously from conventional CT, and investigates whether a physics-informed two-stage cascaded architecture can outperform conventional single-stage networks. Methods Seventy-four head-and-neck cancer patients scanned with a dual-layer DECT scanner were retrospectively analyzed. Integrated detector-layer signals provided SECT-equivalent input images, while DECT-derived maps served as references. Four networks were compared: a single-output UNet (UNet-1), a multi-output UNet (UNet-4), a two-stage cascaded UNet (Cascade-UNet), and the proposed enhanced two-stage cascaded model (Cascade-New), which incorporates an asymmetric encoder-decoder with residual vision modules and Mamba-based dense connectivity, and exploits the physical dependency chain CT → ED/Zeff → SPR through a three-term training loss. Models were evaluated on an independent test set using mean absolute error (MAE), peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR), structural similarity index measure (SSIM), and Pearson correlation coefficient (PCC), with pairwise Wilcoxon signed-rank tests. Results The proposed Cascade-New model achieved the best overall performance: the lowest SPR MAE (11.65 ± 1.58 in units of SPR × 10 -3 vs. 12.99 ± 1.46 for UNet-4, a 10.3% relative reduction), the highest SSIM (0.9971 ± 0.0016), and the strongest correlation (PCC = 0.9996 ± 0.0002). Improvements over UNet-4 in ED, Zeff, and IC synthesis were all statistically significant (all p = 0.031). Visual and error map analyses confirmed its improved performance, particularly in bone and heterogeneous tissue regions. Conclusion This study provides the first demonstration that SPR and other DECT-derived functional images can be synthesized directly from conventional SECT with high precision. The proposed physics-informed cascaded framework offers a cost-effective alternative to DECT, enabling radiotherapy centers to obtain accurate SPR maps with conventional CT for proton dose calculation, potentially reducing range uncertainty and expanding access to high-precision functional imaging.

title: International recommendations for the use of imaging in the diagnosis and assessment of polymyalgia rheumatica.
abstract: Objectives The study aims to develop international recommendations for the use of imaging in the diagnosis and assessment of polymyalgia rheumatica (PMR). Methods An international, multidisciplinary task force of 30 members from 12 countries was convened; the European Alliance of Associations for Rheumatology standard operating procedures were followed. Six clinical key questions addressing the role of imaging (ultrasound, magnetic resonance imaging, and 18 F-fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography) in diagnosis, monitoring, outcome prediction, and technical aspects in PMR were the basis for a systematic literature review. Recommendations were formulated based on evidence and expert opinion and refined iteratively until consensus was achieved. The level of agreement was assessed by voting. Results Three overarching principles and 7 recommendations were developed. PMR remains primarily a clinical diagnosis. Imaging is neither required to confirm PMR in patients with a high clinical probability of the disease nor to exclude PMR in case of low clinical probability. Imaging is most useful in patients with intermediate pretest probability (ie, atypical presentations or suspected alternative/overlapping conditions). No single imaging modality demonstrated sufficient accuracy to be recommended as a first-line test; therefore, imaging should be individualised according to clinical presentation, differential diagnoses, access, and local expertise. Vascular imaging should be performed when overlap with giant cell arteritis is suspected, whereas systematic screening for subclinical vasculitis is not supported by current evidence. Utilising imaging for disease monitoring or outcome prediction is currently not recommended. Conclusions These recommendations provide the first evidence-based guidance for the use of imaging in PMR, reinforcing clinical assessment as the cornerstone of diagnosis and positioning imaging as a context-driven adjunct.

title: Progression of White Matter Hyperintensities in Older Adults: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
abstract: White matter hyperintensities (WMH) are ubiquitous on magnetic resonance images (MRI) in older adults. However, the rate and mechanisms of their proliferation remain unclear, as they are inferred mainly from cross-sectional studies and imperfect single indicators of theoretical constructs. To assess the magnitude of WMH change and its modifiers, we conducted a meta-analysis of 54 longitudinal studies. We found the increase in WMH burden over time (pooled effect size) even in the studies with rigorous participant health screening. WMH proliferation was faster in the samples with higher mean age but independent of sample's sex or ethno-racial composition. Higher prevalence of vascular disease in the sample and lower sample average of diastolic or mean arterial pressure at baseline yielded faster mean WMH progression. Lower baseline cognitive status in samples with healthiest participants was associated with faster WMH increase. Automatic and manual methods produced equivalent results, but manual intervention in automatic methods yielded higher estimates. We found no evidence of publication bias. title: Comparing Short-Term Clinical Outcomes and Survivorship of Complex Revision Total Hip Arthroplasty: Custom Triflange Acetabular Implants Vs Standard Cage Reconstruction.
abstract: Background Complex revision total hip arthroplasty poses challenges in cases of severe acetabular bone loss, pelvic discontinuity, or multiple prior revision total hip arthroplasties. This study compares clinical outcomes and implant survivorship between custom triflange acetabular implants (CTAIs) and standard off-the-shelf cup-cage constructs. Methods Between 2016 and 2022, our registry was screened for consecutive patients who received either a CTAI or an off-the-shelf cup-cage construct. A retrospective review assessed patient characteristics, perioperative data, and postoperative outcomes using radiographs and follow-up notes. Primary outcomes were postoperative mortality and reoperation rates. Secondary outcomes included implant migration, bony remodeling, and patient-reported outcomes using Hip Disability and Osteoarthritis Outcome Score for Joint Replacement (HOOSJR). Kaplan-Meier survival analysis assessed mortality-free survival and implant survivorship. Univariate and multivariate analyses was conducted to determine associations between preoperative variables and postoperative outcomes. Results Among 787 screened patients, 18 met inclusion criteria. Fourteen (78%) had Paprofsky type 3A (28%) or 3B (50%) defects. Eleven (61%) patients received a CTAI, while 7 (39%) received standard off-the-shelf cup-cage constructs. The ΔHOOSJR scores were 37.7 ± 42.4 for off-the-shelf cup-cage constructs and 48.7 ± 30.8 for CTAI, with no significant difference ( P = .531). Two (11%) patients required revision for periprosthetic joint infection, and 4 (22%) expired. Kaplan-Meier survival analysis revealed 75.2% mortality-free survivorship and 78% implant survivorship at 4 years. Conclusions Off-the-shelf cup-cage constructs and CTAIs demonstrated comparable short-term clinical outcomes and implant survivorship in this cohort of patients undergoing complex revision THA. Implant selection may therefore be guided by patient-specific factors and surgeon preference.

title: Reverse Dorr Classification of Lateral Knee Radiographs: A Qualitative Assessment of Bone Quality in Total Knee Arthroplasty.
abstract: Background The Dorr classification is the standard radiographic method for assessing proximal femur bone quality and guiding implant selection in total hip arthroplasty (THA); however, a similar method has not been established for total knee arthroplasty (TKA). Previous studies have demonstrated that radiographic parameters of the distal femur, specifically the ratio of the inner vs outer cortical diameter on lateral knee radiographs, are associated with bone mineral density. The aim of this study was to develop an efficient, reproducible, and qualitative classification system of the distal femur that correlates with bone mineral density to guide implant selection in TKA. Methods A retrospective review of 200 TKA patients with preoperative dual-energy radiograph absorptiometry (DXA) within 1 year of TKA at a single institution was performed. Preoperative lateral knee radiographs were independently reviewed and the degree of anterior cortical taper of the distal femur between the trochlea and a point one patella height (Reverse Dorr 1 [RD1]) or two patella heights (RD2) proximal to the trochlea was graded as Reverse Dorr A, B, or C. Results The Reverse Dorr classification system was associated with DXA T-score, intraoperative physician assessment, and demonstrated moderate to strong interobserver agreement. Reverse Dorr A femurs had a 59-70% predicted probability of normal bone, whereas Reverse Dorr C femurs had a 66-76% predicted probability of osteoporosis. Conclusions The Reverse Dorr classification system is an efficient and reproducible assessment of preoperative bone quality and may serve to inform implant selection in TKA.

title: Integrating the Association Research Circulation Osseous Clinical Practice Guideline into the Diagnosis and Management of Osteonecrosis of the Femoral Head: Four Illustrative Case Scenarios.
abstract: Background Treatment choices for osteonecrosis of the femoral head (ONFH) are based on the patient's age, risk of collapse, lesion size, symptoms, and disease stage. To our knowledge, this represents the first international, evidence-based clinical practice guideline (CPG) developed specifically for the diagnosis and treatment of nontraumatic ONFH, which was recently released by the Association Research Circulation Osseous (ARCO). The CPG offers recommendations that are supported by evidence, but their practical implementation in day-to-day clinical practice may be less intuitive. These case scenarios illustrate the application of the CPG only and do not discuss treatment outcomes, which are discussed in the CPG itself. Methods To illustrate how ARCO CPG recommendations can be applied to a range of ONFH presentations, four relevant clinical cases were chosen. The selection of imaging, evaluation of symptoms, estimation of collapse risk, grounds for observation, use of joint-preserving techniques, and consideration of total hip arthroplasty (THA) are all important diagnostic and therapy choices that are highlighted in each case. Results For small, asymptomatic lesions with little chance of collapse, Case 1 illustrates the value of magnetic resonance imaging in the diagnosis and the suitability of observation. Case 2 shows how core decompression and bone marrow concentrate augmentation can be used to treat symptomatic pre-collapse disease. Case 3 illustrates the decision-making process for a young patient who has bilateral ONFH and needs joint-preserving therapy for the contralateral pre-collapse lesion and THA for one hip with collapse. Case 4 illustrates how patient age, lesion size, and symptom status affect the decision to choose observation over intervention for asymptomatic illness. Conclusion The ARCO CPG provides a practical framework for diagnosis, risk stratification, and treatment selection in patients who have ONFH. Application of the guideline recommendations can facilitate evidence-based and patient-centered decision-making across a broad spectrum of clinical scenarios.

title: Elderly-onset rheumatoid arthritis versus polymyalgia rheumatica: A systematic review and meta-analysis on pathophysiology, diagnosis and clinical progression.
abstract: Elderly-onset rheumatoid arthritis (EORA) and polymyalgia rheumatica (PMR) are among the most frequent inflammatory rheumatic diseases in patients over 50, yet their clinical differentiation, particularly when EORA presents with polymyalgic onset, poses a common diagnostic challenge. This systematic review aimed to identify the pathophysiological, clinical, imaging and treatment-response features that distinguish EORA from PMR. MEDLINE, CENTRAL and Scopus (inception to January 2026), with supplementary searches of LILACS, Google Scholar and trial registries (June 2026) were searched, including studies that compared EORA with PMR or reported separately extractable data for both; risk of bias was appraised with design-specific tools and the evidence weighted accordingly. Seventy-one studies across four domains were included: pathophysiology (22 studies), clinical presentation and final diagnosis at follow-up (24 studies), imaging (21 studies), and treatment response (4 studies). Genetically, in one low risk of bias study that stratified EORA by rheumatoid factor status, PMR and seronegative EORA shared HLA-DRB1*13/*14 associations, a pattern distinct from the shared epitope-driven susceptibility of seropositive RA. However, divergent metabolomic signatures suggest different downstream inflammatory mechanisms. An exploratory random-effects meta-analysis yielded a pooled PMR-to-RA reclassification rate of 7% (95% CI 4-12%; 9 studies), narrowing to 4% (95% CI 2-7%) in methodologically robust studies, though rates of reclassification to RA were considerably higher (up to 20%) when patients with undifferentiated polymyalgic presentations were included. Peripheral arthritis occurred in 28% of PMR patients (95% CI 20-35%; 6 studies), with a significant difference between baseline prevalence (21%) and cumulative incidence over follow-up (34%) on subgroup meta-analysis (p = 0.026), and was characteristically transient and glucocorticoid-responsive, whereas persistent synovitis involving wrists and small joints was associated with reclassification to RA. On imaging, evidence from low-to-moderate risk of bias, ultrasound studies showed that shoulder findings overlapped substantially between conditions, whereas bilateral hip synovitis was significantly more frequent in PMR (47% vs 0% in RA), suggesting the hip as a stronger proximal informative site. However, distal joint synovitis demonstrated the highest discriminatory value, with the presence of at least one among RF positivity, hand grey-scale ≥2, or hand power Doppler ≥1 achieving 89% sensitivity and 93% specificity for EORA identification. This review highlights that the distinction between EORA and PMR cannot be reliably established at a single time point and that longitudinal reassessment integrating clinical, serological, and imaging findings remains essential for the differential diagnosis. However, the evidence is limited by clinical and methodological heterogeneity and the predominance of observational designs.

title: Decoding the Aneurysm Thrombus: Radiomic Signatures of Sac Shrinkage After EVAR.
abstract: Aneurysm sac shrinkage after endovascular aortic repair (EVAR) is a surrogate marker of effective aneurysm exclusion and favorable outcomes. Radiomics enables quantitative imaging analysis beyond visual assessment and is increasingly applied in cardiovascular imaging. Analysis of intraluminal thrombusmay may provide additional information for identifying patients with different patterns of sac remodeling after EVAR. This single-center retrospective study assessed whether radiomic features of the intraluminal thrombus extracted from preoperative computed tomography angiography (CTA), alone and in combination with clinical and anatomical variables, were associated with aneurysm sac shrinkage after EVAR. Patients undergoing elective EVAR for infrarenal abdominal aortic aneurysm were included and stratified according to sac shrinkage at 12-month follow-up. Preoperative arterial-phase CTA scans were analyzed. The aneurysm sac was manually segmented using 3D Slicer, and the intraluminal thrombus was selected as the region of interest. A total of 530 radiomic features were extracted using PyRadiomics with Laplacian of Gaussian filtering. Features were standardized and evaluated using the Wilcoxon-Mann-Whitney test, Pearson correlation filtering, and Akaike Information Criterion-based feature selection. Predictive performance was compared among combined clinical-radiomic, radiomic-only, and clinical-only models. Among 94 patients, 29 showed aneurysm sac shrinkage. Two radiomic features were significantly associated with shrinkage. Younger age (p=0.02), larger aneurysm diameter (p=0.02), and homogeneous thrombus texture were associated with shrinkage, while the absence of COPD was associated with lack of shrinkage. None of the other evaluated clinical or anatomical variables showed a significant association with sac shrinkage. The combined clinical-radiomic model achieved the best performance (AUC 0.76, sensitivity 0.70, specificity 0.75, accuracy 0.73). Preoperative thrombus radiomic features were associated with subsequent sac shrinkage and provided complementary information when integrated with clinical variables. These findings support the potential role of thrombus radiomics in the characterization of sac remodeling after EVAR and warrant validation in larger cohorts.

title: Histological Differentiation of Neovascularisation and Residual Veins in Groin Recurrence.
abstract: Objectives Recurrence in the inguinal region following surgery for saphenofemoral insufficiency remains a major challenge in venous surgery. Histologically, a distinction can be made between residual stump and neovascularization. Using hematoxylin-eosin and Elastica-van Gieson staining, this study systematically analyses samples from recurrent saphenofemoral lesions. Methods Patient demographic data, the clinical CEAP stage, and the Venous Clinical Severity Score were recorded. A preoperative duplex ultrasound was performed. The resected specimens were processed using standard staining methods. During histological examination, a distinction was made between residual venous tissue and neovascularisation. Results A total of 203 samples were available for histopathological evaluation. In the histological evaluation, 197 samples were classified as stump tissue (97.0%) and 6 samples as neovascularization (3.0%). The diagnostic specificity and predictive value of duplex sonography and intraoperative macroscopic classification between residual stump and neovascularisation was limited. Conclusion Residual venous structures represent the predominant morphological substrate of groin recurrences after saphenofemoral surgery. True neovascularisation occurs only in a few cases and should be regarded as a secondary phenomenon rather than a primary cause of recurrence. Surgical precision during the initial intervention may play an important role in recurrence prevention.
