title: Peri-urethral calcifications as a potential biomarker for acute genitourinary toxicity following prostate stereotactic body radiotherapy.
abstract: Background and objectives Peri-urethral calcifications (PUCs) are readily identifiable on planning computed tomography (CT) and may reflect chronic inflammation, fibrosis, and reduced peri-urethral tissue compliance. We evaluated whether baseline PUCs are associated with acute genitourinary (GU) toxicity following prostate stereotactic body radiotherapy (SBRT). Methods We retrospectively analyzed 60 consecutive patients with localized prostate adenocarcinoma treated with definitive SBRT between June 2023 and February 2026. PUCs were assessed on non-contrast planning CT using predefined criteria by blinded observers. The primary endpoint was acute grade ≥ 2 GU toxicity occurring during treatment or within 90 days, graded according to CTCAE v5. Associations with toxicity were evaluated using logistic regression, with Firth penalized regression used for multivariable analysis. Results PUCs were identified in 17 patients (28.3%). Interobserver agreement was high (93.3%; Cohen's κ = 0.84). Overall, 21 patients (35%) developed acute grade ≥ 2 GU toxicity, including three (5%) with grade ≥ 3 toxicity. Acute grade ≥ 2 GU toxicity occurred significantly more frequently in patients with PUCs than in those without PUCs (64.7% vs 23.3%; OR 6.05, 95% CI 1.78-20.51; P = 0.006). After adjustment for baseline International Prostate Symptom Score (IPSS), PUCs remained independently associated with toxicity (adjusted OR 6.90, 95% CI 1.97-27.96; P = 0.002). Baseline IPSS was also independently associated with toxicity (adjusted OR 1.13 per point; P = 0.008). Conclusion PUCs on routine planning CT were independently associated with acute grade ≥ 2 GU toxicity after prostate SBRT. If externally validated, PUC assessment may provide a simple, cost-neutral imaging biomarker for pretreatment urinary toxicity risk stratification.

title: Development and validation of a cumulative risk model and assessment tool for radiation-induced hypothyroidism in head and neck cancer: a multicentre study.
abstract: Objectives Radiation-induced hypothyroidism (RIHT) is a common late toxicity after head and neck radiotherapy. We aimed to develop and externally validate a multimodal Cox model for patient-specific cumulative RIHT risk assessment. Materials & methods This retrospective multicentre study included 1407 patients across four cohorts. The model was developed in the training cohort and externally validated in three independent cohorts. Candidate predictors included CT radiomics, dosiomics, dose-volume histogram parameters, and clinical variables. A multimodal Cox model was developed and used to estimate cumulative risks across time horizons. Temporal risk groups were derived from predicted 3- and 7-year risks. Results A total of 1407 patients (mean age, 55.4 ± 13.8 years; 1027 men) were evaluated and RIHT occurred in 694 (49.3%). The final model integrated three CT radiomics features, four dosiomics features, mean thyroid dose, age and N stage. It achieved C-index/overall AUC values of 0.714/0.765 in the development cohort and 0.725/0.800, 0.680/0.754, and 0.627/0.690 in the three external validation cohorts. Four temporal risk groups had RIHT event rates of 21.7%, 46.1%, 58.3%, and 71.8%, with significant differences in RIHT-free survival (log-rank p < 0.001). The model was packaged as an open-source software tool for individualised risk assessment. Conclusion The externally validated multimodal Cox model provided time-resolved, patient-specific RIHT risk estimates and temporal risk stratification using routinely available radiotherapy-planning data.

title: Gray matter abnormalities associated with long-term opium use: A voxel-based morphometry study.
abstract: Chronic raw opium use can result in opioid use disorder (OUD). Although voxel-based morphometry (VBM) studies have demonstrated decreased gray matter volume (GMV) in heroin-induced OUD, the structural impacts of long-term raw opium consumption remain poorly understood. This study investigated GMV alterations in men with opium-induced OUD and their association with use duration. High-resolution T1-weighted MRI scans were acquired from 28 men with opium-induced OUD (mean use duration 17.89 ± 5.85 years) receiving opium tincture maintenance and 25 age- and education-matched healthy male controls. Whole-brain VBM (CAT12/SPM12) was controlled for age, total intracranial volume, and nicotine use. Analysis used a voxel-level uncorrected threshold of p < 0.05 with cluster-level FDR correction (p < 0.05), along with stricter thresholds (uncorrected p < 0.001, TFCE with FWE), and small-volume correction (SVC). Partial correlation and multiple linear regression investigated clinical associations. Whole-brain analysis identified a left-hemisphere cluster of reduced GMV (cluster-level FDR-corrected p = 0.009). No clusters survived p < 0.001 or TFCE with FWE correction. Reductions in the left insula, inferior frontal gyrus, and parahippocampal gyrus remained significant after SVC. Left insula GMV was negatively associated with duration of opium use (partial r = -0.45, p = 0.027; β = -0.48, p = 0.027 in regression). Prolonged raw opium use is associated with decreased GMV in areas involved in craving and impulse control. Given that the whole-brain findings were not confirmed by more stringent statistical approaches, the results should be considered exploratory and necessitate replication in larger samples.

title: Effectiveness of technology-enabled teleophthalmology and emerging retinal imaging techniques for diabetic retinopathy screening: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: Introduction Diabetic retinopathy (DR) is a major microvascular complication of diabetes and causes preventable visual loss. Technology-enabled screening can extend retinal assessment beyond specialist settings and strengthen screening, referral, and follow-up across diabetes care pathways. Methods We systematically reviewed randomized and non-randomized implementation studies, diagnostic-accuracy and comparative retinal-imaging studies, and economic evaluations of technology-enabled DR screening. PubMed, EMBASE, Cochrane Library, Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar were searched from inception to 23 May 2026 without language restriction. Two reviewers independently performed study selection, data extraction, and risk-of-bias assessment. Random-effects meta-analyses synthesized comparative and proportional outcomes, and GRADE assessed certainty. Results Thirty-three studies were included. Teleophthalmology increased DR screening uptake/completion versus usual care or pre-implementation practice (RR 1.966, 95% CI 1.451-2.664; I 2 = 75.2%) and improved adherence to recommended eye care (OR 2.464, 95% CI 1.477-4.112; I 2 = 66.47%). The pooled ungradable-image rate was 7.4% (95% CI 3.0%-17.1%; I 2 = 59.17%). Advanced retinal imaging showed pooled sensitivity of 97.59% (95% CI 94.50%-100.00%; I 2 = 0%) and specificity of 91.22% (95% CI 78.46%-100.00%; I 2 = 88.7%) for prespecified vascular lesion detection. OCTA demonstrated a pooled eye-level retinal neovascularization detection yield of 63.6% (95% CI 49.9%-75.4%; I 2 = 46.29%). Economic evaluations supported cost-effective or cost-saving technology-enabled screening across assessed health systems. Conclusion Technology-enabled DR care improves screening participation, adherence, and health-system efficiency, supporting integration of teleophthalmology and advanced imaging into scalable diabetes complication-management pathways.

title: The evolving role of cardiac CT: Emerging technologies and clinical impact.
abstract: Cardiac computed tomography (CT) has progressed from a non-invasive test primarily used to exclude obstructive coronary artery disease into a comprehensive cardiovascular imaging platform for coronary artery disease, myocardial disease, valvular heart disease, and structural heart disease. Coronary CT angiography (CCTA) is now endorsed as a first-line test in appropriately selected patients with stable chest pain or suspected chronic coronary syndromes because it can exclude obstructive disease, depict coronary atherosclerotic burden, support preventive treatment, and inform referral for invasive coronary angiography. At the same time, contemporary cardiac CT is moving beyond luminal stenosis. CT-derived fractional flow reserve and myocardial CT perfusion add a functional assessment of ischemia, whereas late iodine enhancement, CT-derived extracellular volume fraction, myocardial strain, and pericoronary fat attenuation index provide information on fibrosis, ventricular mechanics, vascular inflammation, and prognosis. Cardiac CT also has an established role in transcatheter valve therapy, left atrial appendage occlusion, and prosthetic valve assessment by providing a three-dimensional roadmap for device selection, access planning, and complication prediction. Photon-counting detector CT and artificial intelligence are further expanding the capabilities of cardiac CT through higher spatial resolution, spectral quantification, automated segmentation, quantitative plaque analysis, image reconstruction, and structured reporting. This review summarizes the evidence, technical foundations, clinical applications, and implementation challenges of contemporary cardiac CT, with an emphasis on its transition toward a decision-making platform for personalized cardiovascular care.

title: A robust biomarker combining radiomic and CA19.9 information to predict distant relapse-free survival after radiochemotherapy in pancreatic cancer.
abstract: Background The radiomic feature Statistical Percentile 10% (p10%), extracted from [¹⁸F]FDG-PET images, has been previously identified and validated as a robust predictor of distant progression-free survival (DPFS) in unresectable pancreatic cancer (LAPC). This study aimed to maximize its prognostic potential by combining p10% with CA19.9 serum levels and assessing its generalizability across distinct clinical settings. Methods We analyzed 287 LAPC patients treated with chemoradiotherapy (CRT) and a validation cohort of 72 patients enrolled in the CASSANDRA trial (resectable/borderline-resectable PDAC). Cox models combined p10% with CA19.9 levels measured before RT in LAPC patients, and before surgery for CASSANDRA patients. Results p10% was independently prognostic in both cohorts and its integration with CA19.9 significantly improved the prediction. In the LAPC cohort, the combined model achieved C-index=0.71, with median DPFS of 4.0-vs-15.0 months (p<0.0001;HR=3.22). In the pre-surgery setting (CASSANDRA trial), the model showed good rank-order discrimination (C-index=0.65), with median survival of 11.6 months vs not-reached (p=0.0018). However, the calibration slope of 0.54 suggests that absolute risk prediction requires recalibration in the surgical cohort. Conclusions Integrating p10% with CA19.9 provides a broader representation of tumor aggressiveness. The combined biomarkers demonstrate consistent performance across different disease stages supporting their use for treatment personalization.

title: Comparative assessment of ultrasound and bioelectrical impedance analysis for sarcopenia screening in chronic liver disease.
abstract: Background Sarcopenia, primarily defined by low muscle mass (LMM), is associated with worse clinical outcomes in chronic liver disease (CLD). Diagnosis is challenging due to the lack of standardized tools. Ultrasound (US) offers a promising method for muscle mass assessment but requires validation against reference methods like bioelectrical impedance analysis (BIA). Aim To evaluate the correlation and agreement between US- and BIA-based muscle measurements and the accuracy of US in identifying sarcopenia in patients with cirrhosis and a history of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Methods In this prospective observational study, 88 patients with cirrhosis (HCC active or under follow-up) underwent muscle mass assessment by BIA and US of quadriceps and psoas muscles. Analyses included correlations, intraclass correlation (ICC), Bland-Altman plots, and ROC analysis to determine US cut-offs for sarcopenia. Results Quadriceps US indices correlated with BIA-derived ASMM/h² (r = 0.35-0.45, p < 0.01), with high inter-rater reliability (ICC 0.83-0.96). The feather index demonstrated the best discriminative ability (AUROC 0.81, sensitivity 83%, specificity 72%) in this low-prevalence setting. Dual cut-off strategies improved screening value (negative predictive values above 97%). Conclusion Muscle US is a reliable, non-invasive screening tool for sarcopenia (specifically LMM) in CLD patients. Its use can reduce reliance on complex diagnostics, enabling early detection and improved clinical management.

title: A proteome-based classification of paediatric adrenocortical tumours links functional tumour states to clinical outcome and therapeutic vulnerabilities.
abstract: Background Paediatric adrenocortical tumours (pACT) are rare endocrine neoplasms characterised by marked biological heterogeneity and variable clinical behaviour. Current risk stratification relies largely on histopathology and clinical staging, which incompletely capture underlying tumour biology. We aimed to define proteome-based subtypes of pACT and evaluate their biological, clinical, and therapeutic relevance. Methods In this retrospective cohort study, we performed mass spectrometry-based proteomic profiling of 83 pACT and adjacent non-tumour adrenal tissues. Differential abundance analysis, pathway enrichment, consensus clustering, survival analyses, and clinicopathological correlations were performed. A minimal protein classifier was derived using forward feature selection and leave-one-out cross-validation. Cluster-specific therapeutic vulnerabilities were assessed using a curated druggability framework. Findings Tumours displayed profound proteomic differences compared with adjacent non-tumour adrenal cortex, characterised by activation of cholesterol biosynthesis, steroidogenic, MYC, mTORC1, and cell-cycle programs and suppression of extracellular matrix, adhesion, and immune-related pathways. Unsupervised clustering identified four proteome-defined tumour states that only partially overlapped with histopathological diagnosis. These subtypes differed significantly in endocrine phenotype, vascular invasion, Ki67 index, necrosis, and overall survival (log-rank p = 0.00036). Distinct biological programs included stromal-immune-enriched, mitochondrial steroidogenic, IGF/mTOR-driven anabolic, and highly proliferative chromatin-remodelled states. A five-protein classifier (DAAM2, CIP2A, TSC2, PALS2, and P3H1) reproduced cluster assignments with 92.8% leave-one-out cross-validation accuracy. Cluster-specific analyses identified distinct therapeutic target landscapes, including IGF-axis and epigenetic vulnerabilities. Interpretation Proteomic profiling defines biologically and clinically distinct pACT subtypes that provide prognostic information beyond histopathology. This framework enables proteome-based stratification, identifies candidate therapeutic vulnerabilities, and can be approximated by a five-protein classifier. title: NOX4-related ROS couples PET micro- and nanoplastic exposure to JAK2/STAT3 activation in clear cell renal cell carcinoma.
abstract: The potential influence of polyethylene terephthalate micro- and nanoplastics (PET-MNPs) on the progression of clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) remains insufficiently defined. In this study, environmentally derived PET-MNPs promoted ccRCC cell growth, clonogenic capacity, migration, and invasion, and also accelerated tumor development in subcutaneous and orthotopic models. PET-MNP exposure markedly elevated intracellular ROS and H₂O₂ and preferentially increased NOX4 among the NOX family members examined. Silencing NOX4 attenuated ROS and H₂O₂ accumulation and weakened the associated malignant phenotypes both in vitro and in vivo. Functional rescue further showed that wild-type NOX4, but not the catalytically impaired NOX4-P437H mutant, reinstated oxidative signaling and JAK2/STAT3 activation after NOX4 depletion. Transcriptomic analysis of PET-MNP-responsive genes reversed by NOX4 knockdown highlighted JAK-STAT signaling, which was subsequently narrowed to the JAK2/STAT3 branch by protein screening. JAK2 depletion impaired STAT3 Tyr705 phosphorylation, nuclear localization, and transcriptional activity, whereas STAT3 silencing suppressed PET-MNP-induced tumor-promoting phenotypes. Conversely, constitutively active STAT3 partially restored the effects lost after NOX4 depletion. These results define a NOX4-related ROS-JAK2/STAT3 signaling cascade that contributes to PET-MNP-driven ccRCC progression.

title: Circulating tumor DNA-guided therapeutic strategies for metastatic colorectal cancer patients with multiple small pulmonary-limited nodules: A prospective cohort study.
abstract: Background Small pulmonary nodules (SPNs ≤ 2 cm) in metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC) had heterogeneous biology and no evidence-based treatment algorithms. Circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) can detect molecular residual disease (MRD) but lacks prospective validation for treatment guidance in this setting. Methods 70 mCRC patients with exclusively SPNs were assigned to Cohort 1 (≤1 cm) and Cohort 2 (1-2 cm). Tumor-informed ctDNA was detected at baseline, 30 days after optional local treatment or systemic chemotherapy, then every 3 months for 24 months or until progression. Primary endpoint was progression-free survival (PFS). Results Baseline ctDNA positivity was 35.5% in Cohort 1 and 66.7% in Cohort 2. In Cohort 1, baseline ctDNA positivity significantly correlated with shorter PFS (median PFS: 3.2 months vs. 9.2 months, P = 0.013), which was not seen in Cohort 2. Systemic chemotherapy was associated with a five-fold higher ctDNA clearance than local treatment alone (63.2 % vs. 12.5 %, P = 0.033). ctDNA clearance was associated with longer median PFS (12.6 months vs. 6.8 months, P = 0.038). Longitudinally, patients with consistently negative ctDNA had significantly longer PFS than the overall population (median PFS: not reached vs. 9.2 months, P = 0.012). ctDNA better predicted extrapulmonary metastases with a median lead time of 5.5 months (range, 2.8-9.2 months) preceding radiographic confirmation and extrapulmonary metastases predicted poorer PFS than intrapulmonary spread (median PFS: 3.5 months vs. 9.9 months, P = 0.005). Conclusions Longitudinal ctDNA monitoring may provide prognostic information and help identify extrapulmonary progression in mCRC patients with SPNs. These exploratory findings require prospective validation before informing clinical treatment decisions.

title: From staging to changing strategy: [<sup>18</sup>F]FDG PET/MRI's impact on treatment planning in early breast cancer.
abstract: Introduction Accurate staging at diagnosis is essential for optimizing treatment strategies and prognosis in early breast cancer (EBC). [ 18 F]FDG positron emission tomography/magnetic resonance imaging (PET/MRI) is a hybrid imaging modality that enables simultaneous evaluation of locoregional disease and metastatic spread. This study assessed the impact of [ 18 F]FDG PET/MRI on treatment planning in patients with EBC. Methods This unplanned sub-study derives from a prospective, interventional, single-arm clinical trial (SNB vs PET/MRI 2) conducted at San Raffaele University Hospital (Milan) between July 2020 and April 2024 (NCT04829643). Patients with EBC scheduled for primary surgery underwent additional preoperative [ 18 F]FDG PET/MRI. The primary objective was the proportion of patients whose treatment strategy was modified following [ 18 F]FDG PET/MRI findings and multidisciplinary discussion. The secondary objective was the performance of [ 18 F]FDG PET/MRI in detecting multifocal breast cancer compared with standard imaging. Results A total of 264 patients were analyzed. [ 18 F]FDG PET/MRI led to treatment plan modifications 30.7% (81/264, 95% CI: 25.4%-36.5%) of patients. Surgical approach was altered in 23.9% (63/264), while 4.9% (13/264) received primary systemic therapy and 1.9% (5/264) were referred for systemic therapy alone. [ 18 F]FDG PET/MRI showed a sensitivity of 61.7%, specificity of 84.9%, positive predictive value (PPV) of 49.2%, and negative predictive value (NPV) of 90.4% for multifocal disease detection. When combined with standard imaging, PPV increased to 63.6%; sensitivity was 29.8%. Conclusions [ 18 F]FDG PET/MRI substantially influences treatment decisions in EBC, modifying management in nearly one-third of patients. MRI was highly informative for detecting multifocal disease, whereas the potential added value of [ 18 F]FDG PET/MRI may primarily relate to integrated axillary and distant staging. However, its moderate diagnostic accuracy warrants caution to prevent overtreatment.

title: Gastrointestinal ultrasound in systemic sclerosis: A scoping review of current evidence.
abstract: Systemic sclerosis (SSc) is a rare systemic autoimmune rheumatic disease frequently associated with gastrointestinal (GI) involvement. GI manifestations are heterogeneous, may occur throughout the entire tract from the very early stages of the disease and are often associated with a significant burden of symptoms and complications, leading to high morbidity and mortality. Diagnosis often remains challenging due to the lack of sensitive instruments for early detection and the reliance on invasive or expensive diagnostic tools. In recent years, ultrasound (US) has become an increasingly important tool for GI evaluation across a wide range of conditions, including chronic inflammatory bowel diseases, appendicitis and diverticulitis as well as rarer diseases and functional conditions. The aim of this scoping review is to provide an updated overview of the role of gastrointestinal ultrasound (GIUS) in the assessment and monitoring of GI involvement in SSc. A systematic search of MEDLINE and Scopus identified 25 eligible studies. The available evidence is unevenly distributed across the GI tract: thirteen studies addressed the upper GI tract, seven the anorectum, six the gallbladder and five the mesenteric vessels. For each segment, we summarize how US can detect changes in wall structure, vascularization and motility. The evidence base is limited by small, predominantly single-center and cross-sectional studies, heterogeneous acquisition protocols and reference standards and a scarcity of reproducibility data. Further prospective and multicenter studies are therefore needed to validate the role of GIUS, standardize protocols and establish its integration into the clinical management of SSc patients.

title: Discovery of benzoxazole derivatives as novel α-synuclein aggregate ligands with potential for PET tracer development.
abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is the second most prevalent neurodegenerative disorder worldwide, and the abnormal aggregation of α-synuclein (α-Syn) constitutes its core pathological hallmark. Positron emission tomography (PET) imaging of cerebral α-Syn aggregates holds great promise for the early diagnosis of PD. However, the imaging quality critically depends on the ligands with high binding affinity and selectivity for α-Syn aggregates. In this work, we developed a new type of benzoxazole-based α-Syn aggregate ligands via an SPR-based screening. Among them, candidates D15 (K D = 0.12 μM) and D16 (K D = 0.08 μM) exhibited high binding affinities for α-Syn aggregates in vitro and good potency in the SH-SY5Y cellular model and brain tissues from α-Syn PFF-injected PD mouse models, as well as excellent selectivity for tau and Aβ aggregates in rTg4510 and APP23 transgenic mouse brain sections. Thanks to their favorable blood-brain barrier permeability and suitable structures for radiolabeling for PET imaging, these new ligands represent promising candidates for the development of α-Syn PET radiotracers, offering a valuable foundation for the early diagnosis of PD and related synucleinopathies.

title: A liquid fiducial marker for image-guided proton beam therapy of abdominal tumors.
abstract: Purpose This study compared a liquid to solid fiducial markers regarding visibility, artifact characteristics on X-ray imaging and dose perturbation for image-guided proton therapy (IGPT) of abdominal tumors. Additionally, the radio-opaque composition of the liquid fiducial marker was optimized, and the chemical stability after proton beam irradiation was analyzed. Material and methods The fiducial markers inserted into an anthropomorphic abdominal phantom were exposed to X-ray, single-energy computed tomography (SECT), dual-energy CT (DECT) and cone-beam CT (CBCT) to determine contrast-to-noise ratios (CNR) and artifacts. Proton dose perturbation estimations were performed using a Monte Carlo dose algorithm. Chemical stability following proton beam irradiation was assessed with biophysical and optical methods. Results The CNR of the liquid marker with a volume ≥ 100 μl (CNR ≤ 2.69) on 2D X-ray images was superior to the solid markers (CNR ≤ 1.72). The artifact areas (A) and severity in the CT modalities were more pronounced for the solid (e.g. , sect A ≤ 279.4 mm 3 ) than for the liquid fiducial marker (A ≤ 30.5 mm 3 ). Dose mitigation of ≥ 50% in a proton beam was calculated for solid fiducial markers, while the liquid marker less influenced the dose distribution. Increasing radio-opaque content in the liquid prototypes improved visibility (CNR ≤ 2.97) without significantly increasing artifact volume (SECT: A ≤ 40.5 mm3) or dose perturbation. No degradation of the liquid fiducial marker's chemical composition was observed. Conclusion The liquid fiducial marker demonstrated comparable visibility and chemical stability with reduced artifact generation and dose perturbation compared to solid markers, indicating superiority for IGPT of abdominal tumors. Optimization of the liquid marker composition may be considered.

title: The medical physicist's role in the artificial intelligence era: an updated EFOMP curricular and professional framework.
abstract: Purpose Five years after the European Federation of Organizations for Medical Physics (EFOMP) published its first curricular framework for artificial intelligence (AI) in medical physics, the updated core curricula for radiology, radiotherapy and nuclear medicine have incorporated AI as a core competency rather than an addendum, a change consistent with the framework's principal recommendation. This paper examines the resulting educational landscape and defines the next stage of AI competency for the profession. Materials and methods Focus Group 3 of the EFOMP Artificial Intelligence Special Interest Group used a structured, iterative process of expert deliberation combining comparative curriculum analysis, competency mapping, regulatory analysis and iterative expert deliberation within the Working Group. Four primary source documents were analyzed in depth: the 2021 EFOMP white paper and the three updated EFOMP subspecialty core curricula for radiology, radiotherapy and nuclear medicine. The AI-related content of the three curricula was systematically compared against a predefined analytical framework covering scope, depth of treatment, European Credit Transfer and Accumulation System (ECTS) allocation, terminology, regulatory references, and treatment of recent AI developments. Competency gaps beyond the entry-level curricula were identified and articulated in the knowledge-skills-competence format used in EFOMP curricula. The resulting framework was informed by three large-scale surveys of medical physicists conducted in 2020, 2024 and 2025, and underwent iterative review within the Working Group before consultation within the EFOMP community. Results The three updated curricula converge on a shared methodological foundation but diverge in ECTS allocation, coverage of recent AI architectures, and treatment of the EU AI Act, and six competency gaps were identified as common to all three subspecialties. A cross-subspecialty advanced competency framework is proposed, organized into four domains: validation and quality assurance, AI lifecycle management, generative AI and foundation models, and governance. A professional lifecycle model is introduced describing how these competencies should be acquired during specialist training, maintained through accredited continuing professional development, and formally recognized throughout a medical physicist's career. The medical physicist's responsibilities under the EU AI Act are defined, and the proposed framework is translated into practical recommendations for EFOMP, its National Member Organizations, training centers, and individual practitioners. Conclusions The profession's challenge has evolved from demonstrating the importance of AI to ensuring its safe, trustworthy, effective and regulatory-compliant integration into clinical practice, thereby strengthening patient safety and quality of care.

title: Volume-based quantitative assessment of respiratory-induced organ motion in lung cancers.
abstract: Purpose To comprehensively evaluate respiratory-induced organ motion and deformation using volume-based analysis, overcoming the limitations of conventional point-based methods in radiation therapy for lung malignancies. Material and methods The Internal target volume (ITV) and organs at risk (OARs) were delineated on averaged-phase images from 4D-CT datasets of 11 lung cancer patients. Deformable image registration using an enhanced non-parametric algorithm generated deformation vector fields (DVFs) between each respiratory phase and a reference phase. Voxel-level displacements within each structure were statistically analyzed, quantifying ITV and OAR motion via geometric centroid displacement, mean voxel displacement, and 80th/90th percentile displacements. Pearson correlation analysis assessed the relationship between ITV motion and volumetric deformation, while one-way repeated-measures ANOVA evaluated directional consistency of OAR centroid and voxel-average displacements across LR, AP, and SI axes (p ≤0.05). Results Superior-inferior (SI) displacement of ITVs exceeded lateral and AP motion by 2-6 times. Significant centroid-voxel average motion discrepancies in the left lower lobe, right upper lobe, and diaphragm (p = 0.05) indicate limitations of point-based measures. The 80th percentile voxel motion showed potential as a centroid surrogate. Diaphragm and mediastinum deformation reached 60-80 %, with ITV deformation spanning 5-70 %. Motion metrics correlated strongly within structures but weakly with deformation. Conclusion This approach enables comprehensive quantification of respiratory motion, supporting optimized motion management in lung cancer radiotherapy. As conventional metrics fail to capture organ deformation, integrating both motion and deformation assessments is essential for accurately characterizing respiratory-induced target variations.

title: Asymptomatic congenital CMV infection: long-term cognitive outcome and brain imaging findings.
abstract: Background Infants with symptomatic congenital cytomegalovirus infection (cCMV) are at high risk of neurodevelopmental impairments. However, long-term cognitive outcomes in children with asymptomatic cCMV (acCMV) remain unclear. Patients and methods Through universal CMV screening of approximately 20,000 newborns, children with acCMV (n = 36), children with symptomatic cCMV (n = 4), and matched healthy controls (n = 54) were identified and followed prospectively. Brain MRI and neuropsychological assessments were performed in children with acCMV and controls at 6-8 years of age. Results Brain MRI findings were more common in children with acCMV than in controls (14/23, 60.9% vs. 3/31, 9.7%;p < 0.001). Punctate white matter lesions were the most frequent finding and occurred more often in children with acCMV than in controls (10/23, 43.5% vs. 3/31, 9.7%;p 0.004). Ventriculomegaly, cerebellar cortical malformations, and cerebral cortical malformations were less common and occurred only in children with acCMV. Mean full-scale IQ did not differ significantly between children with acCMV (n = 26) and controls (n = 28) (116.91 ± 11.67 vs. 118.68 ± 13.12, p NS), nor did the mean subtest scores. The full-scale IQ in children with acCMV with brain MRI abnormalities (n = 12) did not significantly differ from those without abnormalities (n = 8) (109.67 ± 13.72 vs. 120.75 ± 9.24, p NS). Neither did the mean subtest scores differ between them. Discussion Despite the high frequency of brain MRI abnormalities, predominantly white matter lesions, cognitive outcomes at early school-age did not differ significantly between children with acCMV and controls. Larger studies are needed to confirm these findings and determine the prognostic significance of brain MRI abnormalities in acCMV.

title: Radiolabelled cyclodextrins to detect cervical cancer: a preclinical feasibility study.
abstract: Radiolabelled cyclodextrins targeting prostaglandin E2 (PGE2) seem promising candidates for positron emission tomography (PET)-based molecular imaging of cervical cancer. Here, we evaluated the performance of gallium-68-labelled 2-hydroxypropyl-β-cyclodextrin (HPβCD) and randomly methylated β-cyclodextrin (RAMEB) for the in vivo PET detection of cervical cancer. P-glycoprotein positive (Pgp+) KB-V-1 and P-glycoprotein negative (Pgp-) KB-3-1 cervical carcinoma xenografts of varying sizes (small-, medium-, large-sized) were established and subjected to [ 68 Ga]Ga-NODAGA-HPβCD and [ 68 Ga]Ga-DOTAGA-RAMEB PET imaging followed by ex vivo biodistribution and immunohistochemical (IHC) analysis of PGE2 and Pgp expression. In line with the IHC results, PET data revealed the capability of both radiotracers to reliably detect each tumor types independent of tumor size. Nevertheless, the modest increase in uptake observed with increasing size may indicate enhanced tumor aggressiveness and angiogenic activity. Comparable radiotracer accumulation in MDR-positive and MDR-negative tumors suggests that HPβCD and RAMEB derivatives are unlikely to serve as substrates of Pgp enabling tumor detection across different tumor types. Collectively, our findings demonstrate that radiolabelled cyclodextrins are promising PET tracers for the in vivo detection of cervical cancer, irrespective of tumor size and Pgp expression.

title: Deep learning super-resolution enhances MRI radiomics for predicting placenta accreta spectrum and invasiveness.
abstract: Objectives Placenta Accreta Spectrum (PAS) is a severe obstetric complication. This study evaluated whether retrospective, post-processing deep learning-based super-resolution reconstruction (SR) was associated with improved MRI radiomics performance for predicting PAS and invasive PAS. Materials & methods This retrospective study involved 245 patients who had placental MRI scans at three different institutions. Of these, 158 cases from Institution I for training set and internal validation set, while 34 patients from Institution II and 53 patients from Institution III served as external validation sets. SR using a generative adversarial network (GAN) was applied to generate SR T2WI (SRT2WI). Predictive models for PAS and invasive PAS were developed based on T2WI, SRT2WI, and the SRT2WI-Clinical model. Two radiologists independently diagnosed PAS using T2WI to serve as a reference for evaluating model performance. Model performance was assessed using the area under the curve (AUC), calibration curves, decision curve analysis (DCA), Delong test, and net reclassification improvement (NRI). SHAP values interpreted the models and quantified feature contributions. Results Across all four cohorts, SRT2WI yielded numerically higher AUCs than T2WI, and SRT2WI-Clinical achieved the highest AUCs. For PAS, SRT2WI-Clinical achieved AUCs of 0.953, 0.887, 0.793, and 0.788 in the training, internal validation, and external validation cohorts 1 and 2, respectively (T2WI: 0.738, 0.697, 0.654, and 0.652; SRT2WI: 0.879, 0.820, 0.696, and 0.768). Corresponding AUCs for invasive PAS were 0.895, 0.875, 0.843, and 0.815 (T2WI: 0.774, 0.699, 0.575, and 0.745; SRT2WI: 0.861, 0.794, 0.729, and 0.808). For PAS, SRT2WI-Clinical significantly outperformed T2WI (P < 0.001) and SRT2WI (P = 0.004) only in training, with no significant validation differences. For invasive PAS, it significantly outperformed T2WI in training, internal validation, and external validation cohort 1 (P = 0.003, 0.021, and 0.019, respectively), but not external validation cohort 2 (P = 0.398); comparisons with SRT2WI were nonsignificant. Calibration showed good agreement, DCA favored SRT2WI-Clinical, and SHAP quantified feature contributions. Conclusions The combination of SR and radiomics shows promise for improving the prediction of PAS and invasive PAS. Integrating clinical features may further enhance model performance, supporting its potential clinical utility.

For PAS, SRT2WI-Clinical achieved AUCs of 0.953, 0.887, 0.793, and 0.788 in the training, internal validation, and external validation cohorts 1 and 2, respectively (T2WI: 0.738, 0.697, 0.654, and 0.652; SRT2WI: 0.879, 0.820, 0.696, and 0.768). Corresponding AUCs for invasive PAS were 0.895, 0.875, 0.843, and 0.815 (T2WI: 0.774, 0.699, 0.575, and 0.745; SRT2WI: 0.861, 0.794, 0.729, and 0.808). For PAS, SRT2WI-Clinical significantly outperformed T2WI (P < 0.001) and SRT2WI (P = 0.004) only in training, with no significant validation differences. For invasive PAS, it significantly outperformed T2WI in training, internal validation, and external validation cohort 1 (P = 0.003, 0.021, and 0.019, respectively), but not external validation cohort 2 (P = 0.398); comparisons with SRT2WI were nonsignificant. Calibration showed good agreement, DCA favored SRT2WI-Clinical, and SHAP quantified feature contributions.

Conclusions

The combination of SR and radiomics shows promise for improving the prediction of PAS and invasive PAS. Integrating clinical features may further enhance model performance, supporting its potential clinical utility.

title: Deep learning-based super-resolution reconstruction for improved image quality in shoulder MRI.
abstract: Purpose To compare the image quality of shoulder Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) using three imaging acquisition or reconstruction approaches-Parallel Imaging (PI), Compressed Sensing (CS), and Deep Learning-Based Super-Resolution Reconstruction (SR)-and to evaluate reader-assessed image quality and preference. Methods A retrospective study included 60 patients (27 males, 33 females; mean age 53.67 ± 12.11 years). Shoulder MRI was performed with PI, CS and SR (reconstructed from CS data) across six sequences. Quantitative and qualitative assessments were conducted by experienced observers. Three radiologists selected clinically preferred sequences after a 2-week washout. Consistency and inter-group comparisons were statistically analyzed. Results The quantitative and qualitative assessment between observers showed good consistency. The SR group showed significantly higher quantitative measurements across all six sequences of structures [e.g. SNR: Supraspinatus tendon SR 14.03 (10.60, 20.26), CS 11.87 (8.39, 15.96), PI 8.75 (5.18, 13.51), P < 0.001] than PI and CS. SR images generally showed lower edge rise distance (ERD) values, significant overall differences among PI, CS, and SR (P < 0.01), Qualitative assessment revealed that SR overall differences among PI, CS and SR, with statistically significant differences (P < 0.001). Furthermore, three reader preference results indicated a preference for SR images that all readers preferred SR images (86 %, 92 %, and 93 %). Conclusion Compared to PI and CS, SR significantly improves image quality in shoulder MRI without increasing acquisition time. SR enhances the visualization of fine anatomical structures, providing improved image quality and supporting its potential application in clinical shoulder MRI.

title: Routine pelvic MRI-derived marrow markers for predicting lumbar QCT-defined bone status using chemical shift-encoded fat quantification and radiomics.
abstract: Objectives To evaluate whether pelvic MRI-derived IDEAL-IQ parameters and T1-weighted radiomics can predict lumbar QCT-defined bone status in cancer survivors undergoing routine pelvic oncologic MRI. Materials & methods This secondary analysis within a prospective surveillance cohort included 123 patients with pelvic malignancies who underwent MRI (with IDEAL-IQ) and lumbar QCT within three months. QCT-derived volumetric BMD at T12-L2 served as the reference standard to classify subjects as normal, osteopenia, or osteoporotic. Pelvic MRI-derived PDFF and R2* were measured at the femoral head, femoral neck, and ilium; a radiomics pipeline was built on T1-weighted images. Inter-reader reliability used absolute-agreement intraclass correlation coefficients (ICCs). Discrimination was evaluated with one-vs-rest ROC analysis, and clinical utility was assessed by decision-curve analysis using out-of-fold probabilities from five-fold internal validation for two decisions: osteoporosis versus non-osteoporosis and low bone mass versus normal bone status. Results PDFF increased and R2* decreased with worsening BMD at all sites (P < 0.05), with good inter-reader agreement (single-measurement ICCs, 0.756-0.988; mean-of-three-reader ICCs, 0.903-0.996). In internal validation, T1-weighted radiomics and IDEAL-IQ demonstrated comparable discrimination for three-class bone status (AUC 0.73-0.78). Class-wise analysis showed near-chance discrimination for osteopenia, indicating that the overall macro-AUC was mainly driven by normal-versus-osteoporosis separation. Models incorporating MRI-derived markers showed higher validation macro-AUCs than the simplified age-and-sex clinical baseline. Decision-curve analysis showed positive net benefit for both imaging-based approaches, but between-modality differences were small and should be interpreted cautiously because confidence intervals overlapped. Conclusion Pelvic MRI-derived IDEAL-IQ and radiomics markers showed modest and comparable performance for predicting lumbar QCT-defined bone status. Their discrimination was mainly driven by separation between normal bone status and osteoporosis, whereas osteopenia remained poorly distinguished. These findings support exploratory opportunistic risk flagging rather than complete three-class risk stratification.

title: DuDoTransGAN: Dual-Domain transformer based generative adversarial unsupervised network for metal artifact reduction in paired and unpaired CT.
abstract: Purpose Metal artifacts from implants degrade CT image quality, while supervised metal artifact reduction (MAR) methods require paired clean data that are rarely available clinically. Methods In this retrospective study, we developed DuDoTransGAN, an unsupervised dual-domain generative adversarial network for paired and unpaired training. It was evaluated on a publicly available paired synthetic dataset (SYN; 90,000 training and 2,000 test slices) and a clinical unpaired knee CT dataset (KNE; 19,032 slices from 66 patients; mean age, 55.8 ± 16.1 years; 36 males), including 6,168 slices with metal artifacts. On KNE, two radiologists independently assessed five image-quality aspects using Likert scales, with ratings reviewed by a senior radiologist. Results In the paired SYN experiment, DuDoTransGAN achieved a mean PSNR of 38.19 dB, the highest mean SSIM (0.975), and the lowest mean RMSE (5.65) among unsupervised methods. Performance remained stable with increasing metal-mask size, demonstrating robustness under larger-metal-mask conditions. In the unpaired KNE experiment, inter-rater agreement was excellent (ICC, 0.941). DuDoTransGAN achieved the highest mean scores among unsupervised methods for artifact removal (3.87 ± 0.48), diagnostic value (3.75 ± 0.50), visual effect (3.90 ± 0.36), and detail retention (3.96 ± 0.40), together with a comparable sharpness score (3.87 ± 0.58), and the highest radiologist selection rate (45 % vs 2 %-21 %). Conclusion DuDoTransGAN is an adaptable unsupervised dual-domain MAR framework that performs effectively on paired synthetic and unpaired clinical data, producing high-quality, clinically interpretable CT images in the presence of metallic implants.

title: Automated segmentation-based emergency CT radiomics for predicting functional outcome at discharge and in-hospital post-stroke pneumonia in primary brainstem hemorrhage.
abstract: Background Primary brainstem hemorrhage (PBSH) is associated with high mortality, disability, and uncertain early outcomes. Emergency non-contrast CT (NCCT) is the earliest imaging examination, but conventional assessment may not fully capture hematoma heterogeneity. This study aimed to develop an automated segmentation-based emergency NCCT radiomics framework for predicting poor functional outcome at discharge and in-hospital post-stroke pneumonia (PSP) in PBSH. Methods This retrospective study included 372 patients with PBSH, comprising a training set (n = 182), an internal test set (n = 79), and a temporal internal validation set (n = 111). Hematomas were segmented using a three-dimensional U-Net. Manual and automated segmentation-based radiomics models were compared, and automated segmentation-derived radiomics features were integrated with conventional radiological predictors to construct combined models for poor functional outcome and PSP. Results The automated segmentation-based radiomics model showed comparable performance to the manual segmentation-based model across all three datasets. The combined prognostic model achieved AUCs of 0.926, 0.923, and 0.858 in the training, internal test, and temporal internal validation sets, with higher AUCs and lower Brier scores than the conventional radiological model. The combined PSP model (AUCs: 0.828, 0.742, 0.681) showed no consistent improvement. SHAP identified hematoma classification as the most influential prognostic predictor. Conclusions Automated segmentation-based NCCT radiomics is feasible for early risk stratification in PBSH. The combined prognostic model showed good discrimination and potential complementary value beyond conventional CT assessment. The PSP model remains exploratory and requires further refinement and validation.

title: MRI-derived radiomics for prostate cancer active surveillance: a systematic review.
abstract: Purpose To systematically review MRI-derived radiomic and artificial intelligence models predicting outcomes in men on or eligible for active surveillance (AS) for prostate cancer, and whether reported endpoints permit quantitative synthesis. Method Following PRISMA 2020, we searched PubMed, Scopus, Embase, and Web of Science (2000-September 2026). Two reviewers independently screened, extracted data, and assessed risk of bias (QUADAS-2, PROBAST) and methodological quality (METRICS). Three subgroups were defined: AS selection at diagnosis, baseline detection of clinically significant cancer, and progression during follow-up. Pooling was pre-specified for subgroups with at least four independent cohorts; endpoint equivalence was assessed. Results Seventeen studies across 12 unique cohorts were included. Seven publications derived from two cohorts; 12 independent cohort-level estimates (n = 2703) remained after overlap resolution. Nine publications (four independent cohorts) addressed progression (AUC 0.70 to 0.95), but progression was defined in five non-equivalent ways, from any grade-group increase to composite core-count criteria, precluding quantitative synthesis. Risk of bias was high or unclear in 16 of 17 studies; the median METRICS score was 32.3 % (range 18.9-52.3 %). No study reported external validation or calibration for progression. Conclusions Progression endpoints were heterogeneous and several were of limited clinical relevance. A core outcome set for AS (at least ISUP grade group ≥3 and/or unequivocal radiological progression), followed by multi-centre external validation with a head-to-head comparison against the PRECISE v2 (Prostate Cancer Radiological Estimation of Change in Sequential Evaluation) score, is the priority before clinical use can be considered.

title: Medical image analysis for three-dimensional reconstruction in adolescent idiopathic scoliosis: Imaging inputs, reconstruction methods, validation evidence, and research gaps.
abstract: Adolescent idiopathic scoliosis (AIS) is a complex three-dimensional (3D) spinal deformity. Although standing full-spine radiography remains the cornerstone of clinical diagnosis and longitudinal follow-up, two-dimensional projections cannot fully characterize vertebral rotation, local osseous geometry, or global spatial alignment. In recent years, computed tomography (CT), magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), conventional radiography, EOS/biplanar radiography, 3D ultrasound, and surface imaging have increasingly been integrated with deep learning, statistical shape modeling, and generative approaches, substantially expanding the technical pathways for patient-specific 3D reconstruction in AIS. However, substantial heterogeneity remains across studies with respect to input constraints, target populations, reference standards, and validation endpoints, and the evidentiary boundaries between technical performance, AIS-specific validity, and clinical validity have not been systematically clarified. This review adopted a structured methodological framework and systematically searched the Web of Science Core Collection, PubMed/MEDLINE, and IEEE Xplore, supplemented by forward and backward citation tracking. Study-level evidence was synthesized across imaging inputs, reconstruction tasks, algorithmic paradigms, and validation designs. A total of 115 core studies were included, comprising 32 AIS-specific studies (27.8%), 21 scoliosis-specific or mixed-population studies (18.3%), and 62 studies based on general spinal-image-analysis evidence (53.9%). Based on the reference standards and validation endpoints used, we established a five-level validation framework ranging from image/segmentation-level validation (L1), anatomical-structure-level validation (L2), and clinical-parameter-level validation (L3), to workflow/generalization-level validation (L4) and clinical-translation-level validation (L5). An evidence-gap matrix based on "imaging modality × methodological task" was also constructed. Among the 115 studies, 28 (24.3%) reached a maximum of L1, 49 (42.6%) reached L2, 34 (29.6%) reached L3, and only 4 (3.5%) reached L4; no study met the L5 criteria, and no explicit AIS-specific external validation was identified. Current evidence indicates that CT provides a strong basis for high-fidelity osseous reconstruction, EOS has accumulated relatively continuous AIS-specific evidence for weight-bearing 3D parameter assessment, and 3D ultrasound offers advantages for repeated radiation-free parameter measurement, whereas MRI-based reconstruction and limited-projection 3D recovery remain rapidly evolving fields. The principal challenge has therefore shifted from whether a 3D structure can be generated to whether structural fidelity can be translated into reliable clinical parameters and whether models can generalize consistently across independent AIS populations, imaging systems, and acquisition protocols. Future work should prioritize AIS-specific multicenter validation resources, task-matched 3D reference standards, and a continuous evidence chain linking structural fidelity, clinical-parameter validity, external generalization, and clinical impact, thereby advancing AIS 3D reconstruction from technical feasibility toward trustworthy clinical application.

title: Periprostatic adipose tissue imaging in prostate cancer: Imaging phenotypes, task-specific spatial strategies, and multicompartment integration-a critical review.
abstract: Purpose To appraise how periprostatic adipose tissue (PPAT) is defined, sampled, and evaluated in prostate cancer imaging, with emphasis on spatial strategy, intended clinical use, evidence maturity, and imaging-tissue correspondence. Method We conducted a structured critical review with evidence mapping, supported by PubMed/MEDLINE and Web of Science searches through August 29, 2026, supplemented by prespecified Google Scholar and citation searches. Two reviewers independently screened records. Reports were mapped by imaging strategy, spatial target, clinical task, evaluation design, reproducibility, cohort overlap, and imaging-tissue correspondence. Results The formal evidence set comprised 113 reports, including 63 clinical imaging reports. Strategies comprised morphometry / computed tomography (CT) attenuation (48 reports), tissue-property / compositional imaging (4), PPAT-focused radiomics (4), and interface / multicompartment modelling (7). Quantitative reproducibility was reported in 19/63 clinical reports. Only two reports underwent independent external evaluation, and neither evaluated a PPAT-only model. Biological and translational evidence supported PPAT as a heterogeneous tumour-adjacent compartment, whereas direct spatially matched imaging-tissue validation remained uncommon. Clinical evidence spanned prebiopsy risk refinement, upgrading or active-surveillance reclassification, local extension and surgical planning, prognosis, treatment-related outcomes, and nodal and metastatic assessment; most reports lacked independent evaluation. Conclusions PPAT imaging is best regarded as a set of spatially defined, task-specific phenotypes rather than a single biomarker. Current evidence positions PPAT as a candidate adjunct to established clinical and intraprostatic imaging information. Clinical adoption will require reproducible definitions and measurements, task-matched assessment of incremental value, independent external evaluation, and prospective evidence of decision impact.

title: Photon-counting CT based vestibular aqueduct trajectory analysis for the assessment of Ménière's disease endotypes and hearing loss.
abstract: Background Ménière's disease (MD) is a heterogeneous inner ear disorder, and imaging-based endotype identification may inform prognosis and personalized management. The vestibular aqueduct (VA) is a candidate imaging biomarker, and photon-counting CT (PCCT) offers high-resolution depiction of temporal bone microanatomy. This study evaluated PCCT-derived VA morphometric parameters as imaging biomarkers for MD endotype identification and hearing loss assessment. Methods In this retrospective study, 106 patients (212 ears) underwent temporal bone PCCT and 3.0-T 3D-FLAIR MRI. PCCT parameters included angular trajectory of the VA (ATVA), VA visibility grade, morphologic subtype, midpoint width, VA length, and posterior semicircular canal-posterior fossa distance. Two neuroradiologists independently evaluated all images. Diagnostic performance for six clinically motivated tasks was assessed by AUC with leave-one-patient-out cross-validation (LOPOCV); associations with pure-tone average (PTA) were evaluated by multivariable linear regression with cluster-robust standard errors. Results Interobserver agreement was excellent (ICC, 0.84-0.91). VA visibility grading identified the hypoplastic endotype with an AUC of 0.860 (LOPOCV, 0.812); combined VA morphology and midpoint width distinguished the degenerated endotype with an AUC of 0.784 (LOPOCV, 0.736). Multivariable regression identified ATVA as an independent PTA predictor (β = 0.238, p = 0.023). Conclusions PCCT-derived VA morphometric parameters enabled MD endotype identification despite clinical heterogeneity and were associated with hearing loss severity, supporting their potential role as imaging biomarkers for MD management.

title: Opportunistic screening of hip osteoporosis using Phantom-Less quantitative CT-Derived thoracic volumetric BMD from routine chest CT: A Multicentre, retrospective study.
abstract: Objective To develop and validate diagnostic thresholds for thoracic volumetric bone mineral density (vBMD) derived from routine chest CT scans, and to evaluate the performance of this metric for opportunistic screening of hip osteoporosis (hOP) and hip osteopenia in adults aged 60 years and older. Methods This multicenter retrospective study enrolled 568 patients aged 60 years and older who underwent both non-contrast chest computed tomography (CT) and dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA). Thoracic quantitative CT-derived volumetric bone mineral density (Th-vBMD) was measured using a phantomless quantitative CT (PL-QCT) system. The robustness of the diagnostic model was evaluated through internal validation, including 500-iteration bootstrap resampling. The diagnostic performance of Th-vBMD was compared against the reference hip DXA T-score. Results A total of 568 patients were included. The prevalence of hOP and hip osteopenia was 36.3 % and 42.6 %, respectively. Th-vBMD demonstrated performance with an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.873 (95 % CI: 0.837-0.910). The optimal Th-vBMD threshold for hOP was 85.4 mg/cm 3 , sensitivity 0.851 and specificity 0.864. The optimal threshold for hip osteopenia was 120.7 mg/cm 3 , sensitivity: 0.860 and specificity: 0.811. Logistic regression identified Th-vBMD ≤ 85.4 mg/cm 3 as an independent predictor of hOP (adjusted OR: 26.70; 95 % CI: 16.3-45.0; p < 0.001). Conclusion This study establishes and validates Th-vBMD thresholds derived from routine chest CT for opportunistic hOP screening in elderly. This cost-effective strategy leverages clinical imaging data to identify individuals at osteoporosis risk, facilitating intervention and advancing osteoporosis prevention.

title: Region-specific associations between dual-Layer spectral detector CT-derived carotid plaque parameters and white matter hyperintensity burden in patients with carotid atherosclerosis.
abstract: Objective White matter hyperintensities (WMH) exhibit region-specific characteristics. Whether dual-layer spectral detector CT (DLSCT)-derived plaque parameters associate with WMH burden region-specifically remains unclear. Methods This cross-sectional study enrolled 213 patients with carotid atherosclerotic plaques who underwent carotid CTA and brain MRI within 30 days. Seven DLSCT parameters were measured; WMH was segmented into juxtaventricular, periventricular, deep, and juxtacortical subregions. Multivariable linear regression assessed associations with total WMH burden (FDR correction). Nested models evaluated incremental value. Linear mixed-effects models with region-by-parameter interactions assessed region-specific associations. Results In the primary model (Model 2), Z-Zeff was significantly negatively associated with total WMH burden (β = -0.205, 95 % CI: -0.299 ∼ -0.111, FDR-q < 0.001). Adding Z-Zeff to the clinical model significantly increased explained variance (ΔR 2 = 0.070, p < 0.001, ΔAIC = -15.09), whereas conventional CTA parameters did not (ΔR 2 = 0.001, p = 0.938). Significant region interactions were observed for Z-Zeff, age, and LDL-C. Z-Zeff was negatively associated with all subregions, strongest in periventricular (β = -0.254) and deep (β = -0.172) WMH. Age was most strongly associated with periventricular WMH (β = 0.436). LDL-C and diabetes were associated only with periventricular WMH (β = -0.111 and -0.221, respectively). Conclusion DLSCT-derived Z-Zeff was independently associated with WMH burden in a region-specific manner, with the strongest associations in periventricular and deep white matter, and provided incremental value beyond clinical and conventional CTA parameters. These findings support Z-Zeff as a potential imaging biomarker linking carotid plaque composition to regional cerebral small vessel disease.

title: Incorporating visceral adipose tissue into dual-region deep learning radiomics on CT improves preoperative lymph node metastasis prediction in gastric cancer: A multicenter study.
abstract: Background Visceral adipose tissue (VAT) is associated with tumor progression in gastric cancer (GC), but its added value for predicting lymph node metastasis (LNM) remains unclear. Purpose This study aimed to construct a DR-DLR model that incorporates CT-based features from both VAT and tumor, with the goal of predicting LNM in GC patients, while investigating its biological relevance. Methods 855 GC patients were retrospectively collected across three clinical centers, divided into a primary cohort, one internal test cohort, and two independent external validation cohorts. An Attention Residual Transformation Network (ARTNet) extracted imaging representations from CT images. Feature representations and clinical variables were integrated using a multilayer perceptron (MLP) to build the DR-DLR model. Model performance, generalizability, prognostic value, and biological relevance were evaluated using internal/external testing, radiologist comparison, survival analysis, and radiogenomics analysis. Results Incorporation of VAT-derived features improved predictive performance compared with tumor-only models. The DR-DLR model achieved areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.898 (95 % CI: 0.817-0.946), 0.834 (95 % CI: 0.743-0.897), and 0.848 (95 % CI: 0.775-0.901) in the internal and two external test cohorts, respectively. It outperformed junior and senior radiologists in LNM assessment. Overall survival was shorter in high-risk patients than in low-risk. Radiogenomics analysis revealed that the high-risk phenotype was associated with activation of immune-related pathways and increased infiltration of CD4 + T cells, plasma cells, dendritic cells, and mast cells. Conclusion The DR-DLR model improved LNM prediction, with its high-risk phenotype linked to immune-related molecular alterations, supporting its value for preoperative risk stratification.

title: CT-based multimodal fusion model for preoperative clear cell renal cell carcinoma grading: A multicenter study.
abstract: Objectives To develop and evaluate a multimodal fusion framework for the preoperative World Health Organization/International Society of Urological Pathology (WHO/ISUP) low- and high-grade classification of clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC), integrating clinical characteristics, deep learning (DL), and radiomic signatures extracted from corticomedullary phase (CMP) contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CECT) images. Materials and methods In this retrospective multicenter study, we evaluated a cohort of 1,052 patients with histologically verified ccRCC across four institutions. The data of the primary cohort (Center A, n = 665) were randomly divided into a training dataset (n = 465) and an internal validation dataset (n = 200). The data of 387 additional patients from three institutions (Centers B-D) constituted the independent external test set. Initial single-modality classifiers were developed via ensemble machine learning, utilizing clinical variables, multiscale radiomic data (capturing intratumoral, habitat, and peritumoral regions), and DL representations (2D, 2.5D, and 3D). A soft voting mechanism was subsequently applied to integrate the top-performing base models. Model interpretability was determined using SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) values, and overall diagnostic efficacy was quantified through receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis. Results The weighted soft voting model (SoftVote-Opt) showed the numerically highest AUC among the evaluated fusion strategies and single-modality models. This model yielded AUCs of 0.761 (95 % CI: 0.675-0.839) and 0.745 (95 % CI: 0.675-0.813), with corresponding MCCs of 0.347 (95 % CI: 0.217-0.475) and 0.302(95 % CI: 0.205 -0.387), within the internal validation and external test sets, respectively. SHAP analysis revealed peritumoral 5 mm radiomic features as the primary determinants of the model's output, followed by intratumoral radiomic features, whereas deep learning and clinical features offered lower relative contributions. Conclusion The multimodal fusion framework demonstrated moderate discriminatory performance across the internal validation and external test cohorts. These findings could be regarded as an exploratory study rather than evidence of established clinical superiority. The framework may provide complementary information for preoperative ccRCC grading. Critical relevance statement This study evaluates an exploratory multimodal fusion framework for preoperative ccRCC grading by combining clinical data, deep learning, and multiscale radiomic features. The framework may provide complementary non-invasive information for risk stratification.

title: Toward truly agentic radiology AI: A multimodal architecture framework and differentiated implementation roadmap.
abstract: Agentic artificial intelligence(AI) represents a structural transition from task-specific tools to autonomous systems capable of goal-oriented, multi-step reasoning. However, translating this potential into radiology requires a fundamental shift from text-dominated architectures to avision-first approachthat engages the specialty's diagnostic core. In this paper, we characterize the multimodal challenge distinguishing radiology from text-centric domains, where high-dimensional images serve as the primary diagnostic substrate rather than supplementary data. We reviewthree image-text coupling architectures, their clinical capabilities, limitations, and deployment feasibility. These include output-level coupling through sequential image-text pipelines, representation-level coupling through contrastive aligned dual encoders, and token-level coupling through generative vision-language models. To guide development, we introduce afive-level taxonomy of autonomy(Levels 1-5), establishing clear validation checkpoints and regulatory expectations for increasing machine independence, from text-based workflow automation to fully autonomous closed-loop systems. We emphasize that interoperability via standardized protocols, includingDICOMweb, HL7-FHIR, Model Context Protocol (MCP), and Agent2Agent (A2A), is as critical as the AI models themselves. Finally, we address critical implementation guardrails, including mitigatingalgorithmic hallucinations, defending againstadversarial prompt injection, and preserving human diagnostic proficiency amidst the risk of AI-induced skill decay. This comprehensive roadmap provides a structured path for integrating autonomous visual reasoning into modern medical imaging environments.

title: Ultra-high-resolution 5 T MR neurography: first steps.
abstract: Magnetic resonance neurography (MRN) is an established technique for peripheral nerve assessment, enabling high-resolution visualization of nerves and simultaneous evaluation of adjacent musculoskeletal structures. Although optimized 3 T MRI remains the clinical standard, whole-body 5 T systems have emerged as a potential intermediate platform between 3 T and 7 T imaging. Direct peer-reviewed evidence for peripheral MRN at 5 T remains limited to a single pilot study of the inferior alveolar nerve, with no prospective validation of the brachial plexus, lumbosacral plexus, or limb nerves. Physical and engineering studies suggest that 5 T MRI may provide greater signal availability than 3 T while presenting less severe radiofrequency-related challenges than 7 T; however, the relevance of this theoretical balance to peripheral nerve imaging remains unproven. The additional signal available at 5 T could theoretically be allocated to higher spatial resolution, greater acceleration, or broader anatomical coverage, but these potential gains have not been validated against optimized 3 T MRN. Potential applications include the evaluation of entrapment neuropathies, traumatic nerve injuries, inflammatory neuropathies, peripheral nerve tumors, and the implementation of quantitative approaches such as diffusion tensor imaging, T2 mapping, and T1ρ imaging. Furthermore, artificial intelligence-based reconstruction, denoising, and acceleration strategies may improve the clinical feasibility of ultra-high-resolution neurography by reducing scan times while preserving image quality. This narrative review examines the limited published evidence, physical rationale, technical requirements, preliminary institutional experience, and research priorities for 5 T MRN.

title: Pancreatic mucinous cystic neoplasms in adults: An update on the role of CT and MRI for risk stratification.
abstract: Pancreatic mucinous cystic neoplasms (MCNs) are characterized histologically by an inner mucin-producing columnar epithelium supported by a dense ovarian-type stroma. MCNs account for approximately 10% of pancreatic cystic neoplasms. Surgical resection is the treatment of choice, as MCNs may harbor high-grade dysplasia or progress to invasive carcinoma. Establishing reliable imaging criteria for risk stratification is critical to identify patients who are candidates for surgery. Computed tomography and magnetic resonance imaging play pivotal roles in lesion characterization and assessment of features associated with high-grade dysplasia or invasive carcinoma. Current guidelines recognize several imaging features as high-risk characteristics for MCNs, including large tumor size, mural nodules, and main pancreatic duct dilatation. However, other potential predictors of malignancy remain poorly defined and are not sufficiently emphasized. The strongest MCN-specific evidence, as demonstrated in multivariable analyses, supports larger cyst size, mural nodules, main pancreatic duct dilatation, and, in selected cohorts, elevated serum cancer antigen 19-9. Male sex has also been associated with malignancy in retrospective surgical cohorts, whereas pancreatic head/neck location, calcification, wall/septal thickening, age, and signal heterogeneity on T2-weighted images remain less consistently validated. Importantly, most malignancy-prediction literature is based on resected, pathologically confirmed MCNs and is therefore vulnerable to selection and verification bias and cannot be directly extrapolated to all incidentally detected presumed MCNs. This article presents a transparent literature search methodology and an evidence-based synthesis of predictors of malignancy that clearly distinguishes MCN-specific multivariable evidence from lower-level or extrapolated data. It also provides a comparison of key guidelines. Unlike previous reviews, this article directly addresses the evidence gap between resection-based cohorts and the broader population of incidentally detected presumed MCNs. It also clarifies when imaging findings should prompt further evaluation rather than independently determine management.

title: Background parenchymal enhancement in ultrafast MRI: Inter-reader agreement before and after training, and correlations with prognostic factors of breast cancer.
abstract: Purpose To assess the inter-reader agreement in background parenchymal enhancement (BPE) categorization on ultrafast dynamic contrast-enhanced (DCE) MRI before and after training and its relationship with breast cancer prognostic factors. Materials and methods We retrospectively analyzed the cases of 220 patients (median, age 60 years; 220 breast cancers) who underwent ultrafast DCE MRI. BPE was qualitatively classified as minimal, mild, moderate, or marked by three readers: Reader1 (R1), a radiology resident in the second year of training; Reader2 (R2), an experienced general radiologist with 28 years of experience in diagnostic radiology; and Reader3 (R3), an experienced breast radiologist with 25 years of experience in breast MRI. Inter-reader agreement was evaluated using weighted kappa (κ) values and was reassessed between R1 and R3 after intensive training. Associations between BPE levels and prognostic factors were also evaluated. Results Inter-reader agreement was substantial with weighted κ values of 0.679-0.742 for R1 versus R2, 0.612-0.665 for R1 versus R3, and 0.626-0.689 for R2 versus R3. Agreement between R1 and R3 improved slightly after training but remained substantial. No significant associations were observed between visual BPE classification and prognostic factors, including hormone receptor status, HER2 status, and proliferation markers. Conclusion Inter-reader agreement for BPE assessment on ultrafast DCE MRI was substantial and improved slightly after training. No significant relationship was observed between ultrafast BPE and breast cancer prognostic factors.

title: An integrated pathological-radiological downstaging score for prognostic classification in gastric cancer after neoadjuvant chemotherapy: A multicenter retrospective study.
abstract: Background Neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NAC) followed by surgery is the standard treatment for locally advanced gastric cancer (LAGC). However, post-therapy staging based on ypTNM mainly reflects residual pathological status and does not capture pretreatment disease burden or the extent of tumor regression after NAC, limiting postoperative prognostic stratification. To address this limitation, we developed a Pathological-Radiological Integrated Model (PRIM) that combines baseline stage, post-treatment pathology, and radiologic response. Methods We enrolled 414 patients with LAGC who underwent radical gastrectomy after NAC, including 348 in a development cohort and 66 in an external validation cohort. A Down-stage System (DS) was constructed to quantify tumor stage changes after NAC by weighting cT/cN and ypT/ypN categories using multivariable Cox regression. DS was then combined with RECIST response to establish the PRIM system. Prognostic performance and clinical utility were evaluated and compared with conventional ypTNM staging. Results PRIM stratified patients into four distinct risk groups with significantly different 3-year overall survival rates (86.9%, 69.9%, 40.0%, 21.2%; P < 0.001). Compared with ypTNM, PRIM demonstrated improved prognostic performance, with a higher C-index (0.728 vs. 0.696, P < 0.001), AUC (0.775 vs. 0.731, P < 0.001), and better model fit (AIC: 1471.62 vs. 1509.33; BIC: 1474.61 vs. 1512.32). Risk reclassification was also improved (NRI 14.49%; IDI 8.9%). Time-dependent ROC analysis showed consistently higher predictive accuracy for PRIM over 5 years. Conclusion By integrating pathological and radiological response information, the PRIM classification provides improved postoperative prognostic stratification compared with ypTNM alone in patients with LAGC treated with NAC.

title: Core Descriptor Set for Studies Evaluating Interventions for Chronic Deep Venous Diseases.
abstract: Objective Chronic deep venous disease (CDVD) is a common and debilitating disease resulting in significant morbidity and costs. However, inconsistent reporting of patient characteristics in CDVD hinders study comparability and limits opportunities for data synthesis. This study aimed to develop a core descriptor set (CDS) for studies evaluating interventions for CDVD of the lower limbs. Methods Candidate descriptors were identified from published literature and stakeholder recommendations. Vascular surgeons, haematologists, interventional radiologists, and nurse specialists took part in two rounds of an international modified Delphi process using a nine point Likert scale to rank descriptor importance. Descriptors not meeting consensus criteria in the first round were re-evaluated in round two. Descriptors meeting the criteria for critical importance were discussed in a final meeting between international specialists to finalise the CDS. Results One hundred and thirty-eight Delphi participants were recruited from 29 countries. Ninety-eight descriptors were longlisted from the literature, refined to 84 by the steering group. After round one, 23 descriptors achieved consensus and were removed from subsequent rounds. Seven newly proposed descriptors were then added, resulting in a total of 68 descriptors in round two. Following round two, a further 13 descriptors achieved consensus with eight considered borderline. Following two Delphi survey rounds and a consensus meeting, 84 candidate descriptors were systematically evaluated and narrowed down to a final set of 21 core descriptors across the domains of demographics, thrombotic risk, venous history, anatomy, symptoms, and clinical findings. Conclusion This study defined the CDS for CDVD, facilitating more consistent, robust, and meaningful reporting across studies and enabling reliable synthesis.

title: Nursing management of postoperative hemorrhagic shock: A case study in intensive care.
abstract: Introduction Postoperative hemorrhagic shock is a time-critical complication associated with high morbidity and mortality, particularly in older surgical patients, requiring rapid, coordinated management in the intensive care unit (ICU). This case report describes specialized nursing management guided by the International Classification for Nursing Practice (ICNP®/CIPE®) and Benner's Clinical Wisdom Theory. Case presentation An 89-year-old woman underwent emergency gastrojejunostomy for intestinal obstruction and subsequently developed hemorrhagic shock with profound anemia (hemoglobin nadir 5.8 g/dL), severe hyperlactatemia (12 mmol/L), hypothermia (33.6 °C), peripheral hypoperfusion, and hypotension (mean arterial pressure <65 mmHg). She required orotracheal intubation, invasive mechanical ventilation, and deep sedation. Diagnostic reassessment included serial hemoglobin and arterial blood gas analyses, lactate trending, invasive hemodynamic monitoring, and surgical re-exploration with intraoperative upper endoscopy, which suggested an upper gastrointestinal source (suspected Mallory-Weiss type lesion) treated endoscopically. Nursing priorities, structured using ICNP®, focused on perfusion restoration and correction of the lethal triad (hypothermia, acidosis, coagulopathy), multimodal analgesia, continuous monitoring, prevention bundles (infection and pressure injury prevention), and structured family communication. Discussion The patient progressively stabilized, with hemoglobin increasing to 9.6 g/dL, lactate decreasing to <1 mmol/L, normothermia recovery, discontinuation of vasopressors, and no documented ICU-acquired complications during the ICU stay. This case highlights how standardized nursing language (ICNP®/CIPE®), combined with advanced clinical reasoning and evidence-based ICU bundles, can improve the structure, traceability, and continuity of nursing care in postoperative hemorrhagic shock.
